#2099. The Good, The Bad and The Ugly of Scott Parker’s Managerial Career

With Scott Parker now in the manager’s seat, supporters are naturally asking the same question: what exactly will a Parker team look like?

Last night gave us a glimpse of his ability to deliver a rousing half-time team talk, but what else can he bring to the table besides a penchant for pricey cardigans?

His managerial career has established a clear tactical identity, one that has delivered success in the Championship but has also attracted criticism at higher levels.

Gonzo has already covered this in a previous article, citing that Parker typically favours either a 4-2-3-1 or 4-3-3 formation, built around organisation, possession and defensive discipline.

His teams are usually constructed from the back, with an emphasis on retaining control of the ball rather than engaging in frenetic, end-to-end football. The objective is often to dominate territory through patient build-up play, moving possession into wide areas to stretch opponents before creating openings.

Defensively, Parker’s sides tend to be compact and difficult to break down. A double pivot in midfield frequently provides protection for the back line, allowing his teams to maintain their shape and reduce space between the lines.

The philosophy is clear: control games first, take risks second.

While that approach has often proved effective in the Championship, critics argue it can sometimes become overly cautious, particularly when chasing games or facing stronger opposition.

One aspect of Parker’s CV cannot be ignored: he knows how to get out of the Championship.

He guided Fulham to promotion through the play-offs in 2020 and followed that by leading Bournemouth to automatic promotion in 2022. His ability to organise teams over the course of a demanding Championship season is well established.

For a West Ham side whose only objective is a return to the Premier League, that experience was undoubtedly a major factor behind the club’s decision.

The bigger question is whether he can combine results with the attacking football supporters crave.

Will Parker get West Ham on the front foot?

At Fulham, supporters generally look back on Parker’s spell with a degree of respect.

Promotion to the Premier League remains a significant achievement, but frustration grew during the following campaign as the football became increasingly conservative. Despite periods of decent organisation, Fulham were ultimately relegated and some supporters felt the team’s cautious approach limited its potential.

With regards to his time at Bournemouth, Parker’s stock was initially high on the south coast after guiding the club back to the Premier League at the first attempt.

However, his relationship with supporters deteriorated rapidly following promotion. Public criticism of the club’s transfer business and squad depth, particularly after a heavy 9-0 defeat at Liverpool, created tensions that cost him his job.

His dismissal divided opinion, especially after Gary O’Neil kept Bournemouth comfortably in the Premier League with largely the same group of players.

Parker’s short tenure in Belgium at Club Brugge proved to be the most difficult period of his managerial career.

Expectations were high upon his arrival, but results and performances failed to follow. His tactical approach was widely criticised and he struggled to adapt quickly enough to the demands of Belgian football.

The experiment was brought to an abrupt end after only a brief spell in charge.

Burnley supporters largely viewed Parker’s appointment through a practical lens.

His track record of Championship promotions offered reassurance, but concerns remained over whether his style could provide the excitement and attacking intent fans wanted to see.

As with many clubs that have employed Parker, appreciation for results was often balanced against questions surrounding entertainment value.

That said, I actually know a Burnley fan, and when Parker was appointed, he messaged me just two words: “Good appointment!”

The challenge facing Parker at West Ham is clear. We arguably possess one of the strongest squads in the division and supporters will expect more than simply grinding out results. Promotion remains the priority, but fans will also want to see an identity return to the team after the uncertainty of the Nuno Espírito Santo era.

One thing is certain: after months of instability, West Ham have turned to a manager with a proven track record at this level.

Now comes the difficult part. Turning potential into winning games!

Now he’s in, let’s unite behind him and see where he can take us. COYI!

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

Our current goalkeeper has not laid a hand on the last nine goals he has let in. Virtually every corner if he makes a parry out, it is always at 90 degree angle to our goal, so making an assist for the opposition, who have gone on to score from this assist. Ex professional goalkeeper Nuno, could not help this boy change his bad habits, surely Scott has already realised changes start with the goalkeeper

Scott’s style of play will have to be adapted to utilise to the full the talents of this current squad.

This will be a totally bespoke solution to the formation conundrum. Scott is up to the task in hand. When he had gained promotion with the other three teams, they sold his best players and expected him to work miracles whilst remaining silent about the circumstances.

Considering the rug-pulling, Scott did a great job at each club. With some support to enhance and progress the playing staff available to him he would have been well established as a leading PL manager by now.

I still believe he has the attributes to be that leading PL manager and I hope that will be whilst in the employ of West Ham.

#2097. Man United transfer news: Three strikers Red Devils could sign in January following Benjamin Sesko injury update

By Matt Law | 04 Nov 2026 16:53, Last updated: 04 Nov 2026 16:56

Manchester United could enter the January transfer window for a new striker, with Benjamin Sesko's ongoing shin problem a serious concern for the club.

Sesko is expected to be out until the start of 2027 with the shin injury that he initially suffered towards the end of the 2025-26 campaign.

Bryan Mbeumo is operating through for the middle for Man United at this moment in time, but the Cameroon international is better off the right.

Joshua Zirkzee is an option, but the Netherlands international continues to struggle to make his mark for the 20-time English champions.

Here, Sports Mole looks at three strikers who could be signed by Man United in January to hand themselves a major boost for the second half of the season.

Man United are currently being linked with a move for Calvert-Lewin, who has scored five goals in 11 appearances for Leeds during the 2026-27 campaign.

The 29-year-old made the move to Elland Road on a free transfer in the summer of 2025, and the striker has been impressive for Leeds, netting 20 times in 50 appearances for the club.

Calvert-Lewin is proven in the Premier League, scoring 75 times in 283 appearances in the competition, while he has also scored four times in 14 caps for England.

Man United would not have to break the bank to sign Calvert-Lewin, although it would not be a straightforward deal given the rivalry between the Red Devils and Leeds.

Calvert-Lewin scored against Man United in the Premier League earlier this season, and it is understood that the 20-time English champions are admirers of his talents.

Toney's future is again the subject of speculation, with the England international potentially a loan option for Man United at the start of 2027.

The 30-year-old has been in impressive form this season, scoring 14 goals and registering two assists in 15 appearances in all competitions for his Saudi club.

Toney made the move to Al-Ahli from Brentford in the summer of 2024, and his record for his current team stands at 86 goals and 19 assists in 108 appearances.

The forward scored 72 goals in 141 matches for Brentford, including a record of 36 goals in 83 games in the Premier League.

The Englishman is not a long-term option for Man United but could be an ideal short-term signing given that he is proven in the Premier League.

Toney might also feel that he has unfinished business in England's top flight.

Mateta's contract at Palace is due to expire at the end of the campaign, and there are currently no indications that he will be signing a fresh deal.

The 29-year-old has had a frustrating season to date due to injury, while he was sent off in Palace's last Premier League game against Tottenham Hotspur.

Mateta has scored 63 goals and registered 14 assists in 207 appearances for Palace in all competitions, including 50 goals and nine assists in 166 Premier League matches.

The Frenchman is seemingly looking for a way out at Palace and is said to be keen to explore a switch to the 20-time English champions next year.

A loan move for the striker is unlikely given his contract situation, but he could potentially be available for a bargain transfer fee in the winter market.

#2096. Blackburn Rovers vs West Ham Preview & Lineups – Five Changes For Parker?

Blackburn Rovers v West Ham United EFL Championship Ewood Park Saturday 7 November 2026, 3pm GMT

Scott Parker had less than 24 hours to prepare West Ham United for Wednesday night’s extraordinary 3-3 draw at Cardiff City, but the second-half transformation should heavily influence the team he selects against Blackburn Rovers.

The Hammers were unrecognisable after the interval, recovering from three goals down through Divine Mukasa, Arne Engels and Max Kilman. Parker, Mark Noble and Jarrod Bowen clearly delivered a rousing half-time message, while the tactical and personnel changes completely altered the match.

West Ham remain eighth and four points behind second-placed Wolverhampton Wanderers, making victory at Ewood Park extremely important. Parker will have the international break to properly implement his methods, but first he must use the lessons from Cardiff to select a side capable of taking three points into it.

I have already covered the Cardiff match extensively, so there is little value in going over every detail again. What matters for this preview is the enormous contrast between West Ham’s two performances.

I very much detach the three goals conceded in the first half from what happened after the break. The opening 45 minutes looked like a continuation of everything we had witnessed under Nuno Espírito Santo, while the second offered the first glimpse of Parker’s influence.

Parker introduced Ezra Mayers, Mohamadou Kanté and Joël Piroe at half-time before later replacing Manor Solomon with Edvin Austbø. Those decisions gave West Ham greater energy, aggression and bite.. in short, the changes worked an absolute treat.

The substitutions worked, but so did the tactical changes. West Ham pressed higher, attacked space behind Cardiff’s defence and played with an urgency which had been completely absent before the break. As I discussed in my reaction to Parker’s first post-match interview, the new manager was particularly enthusiastic about the more aggressive, front-footed approach.

That should influence Parker’s selection at Blackburn far more than anything he can achieve during two brief training sessions.

Engels & Piroe can both expect to start against Blackburn

I think it is time to give Mads Hermansen a rest and select Alphonse Areola in goal. Hermansen has endured a difficult period, conceding nine times across the past three matches, and temporarily removing him from the firing line may benefit everybody.

Parker already knows Areola extremely well from their season together at Fulham. The goalkeeper was brought to Craven Cottage during Parker’s time as manager and performed impressively despite their eventual relegation.

That existing relationship could make this an obvious early change. Parker knows Areola’s strengths and temperament, while the goalkeeper will understand what the new head coach expects from him.

Replacing Kyle Walker-Peters is straightforward if he remains unavailable. Joël Veltman was sensational during the second half at Cardiff and should continue at right-back.

Veltman provided leadership, composure and attacking support for Bowen. At a time when West Ham’s defence has looked incredibly nervous, his experience is particularly valuable.

Mavropanos returned from his knee problem on Wednesday and should remain alongside Kilman. The partnership still needs work, but Parker has very little time to experiment before the international break.

The significant change should come at left-back. Ezra Mayers impressed again after replacing Morato at half-time and deserves an opportunity from the beginning.

Mayers offered more natural movement down the flank and was willing to attack the penalty area. He almost completed the comeback with a late volley and looked considerably more comfortable in the position than a centre-back being asked to operate as a full-back.

I do not see how Tomáš Souček can force his way into the starting XI. He nearly scored the winner at Cardiff with a late header, but both Engels and Mukasa deserve to retain their places.

Engels improved enormously after half-time and took his goal like a striker, timing his run perfectly before producing a confident finish. Mukasa also deserves to continue in his preferred attacking-midfield role after scoring West Ham’s first and helping change the momentum of the game.

Kanté has absolutely forced himself into the team. His energy, ball-carrying and aggression transformed the midfield, giving West Ham the ability to press Cardiff and move possession forward quickly.

The most sensible balance is therefore Engels and Kanté as the two deeper midfielders, with Mukasa ahead of them. Souček remains an excellent option from the bench, particularly when West Ham need a goal or greater aerial presence late in a game.

Joël Piroe must start in attack. His clever flick created Engels’ goal, but his overall movement and willingness to drop deeper also helped connect West Ham’s midfield with the forward line.

Piroe is the only recognised striker in the squad with a proven Championship goalscoring record, yet he has not received a consistent run of starts. Parker should now give him the opportunity to establish himself.

Austbø also deserves to replace Solomon on the left. The Norwegian was direct and positive after coming on, forcing a late save and immediately looking more dangerous than the player he replaced.

Bowen will naturally continue on the right, although Parker should allow him to drift into central areas. The captain ran the second half at Cardiff, creating all three West Ham goals and dragging the team back into a match which had appeared completely lost.

I expect Parker to retain the 4-2-3-1 formation but reward the players who changed the game at Cardiff. Areola, Mayers, Kanté, Austbø and Piroe should all come into the starting XI.

Blackburn have lost consecutive matches against Swansea City and Stoke City, but their victory over current leaders Middlesbrough demonstrates that West Ham cannot take them lightly.

Tony Mowbray’s team have won five Championship matches this season and will be determined to enter the international break with a response of their own. Ewood Park has not been a regular destination for the Hammers, with this our first league visit since the 2010/11 Premier League season.

Nevertheless, West Ham should travel north with genuine confidence following the Cardiff comeback. Parker now has evidence of which players responded to his instructions and which combinations gave the team greater balance.

This is his final match before receiving two uninterrupted weeks on the training pitch. A victory would reduce the gap to the automatic-promotion positions and give him valuable momentum before beginning the more substantial work of reshaping the team.

Blackburn’s recent defeats suggest this is an excellent opportunity for Parker to claim his first victory as West Ham head coach. The Hammers must still defend considerably better, but the second-half attacking performance at Cardiff showed what this squad can produce.

If Parker selects the players who drove that comeback and retains the more aggressive approach, I believe West Ham will have too much quality for Blackburn. There may still be another defensive mistake in this team, but I expect the Hammers to win convincingly enough.

Prediction: Blackburn Rovers 1-3 West Ham United

#2094. Scott Parker Wants More Of What Nuno Couldn’t Deliver At West Ham

West Ham manager Scott Parker has given supporters an early indication of the football he wants to play, and if his comments following Wednesday night’s extraordinary comeback against Cardiff City are anything to go by, I’m all for it.

The new Hammers boss has made no secret of his admiration for the team’s second-half performance, when West Ham recovered from three goals down to draw 3-3. Speaking ahead of Saturday’s trip to Blackburn Rovers, Parker described the aggressive, attacking football he witnessed as precisely the sort of performance he wants to reproduce.

Now, I’m keen not to read too much into what was, in essence, just 45 minutes of football. We’ll certainly learn considerably more about Parker’s tactical intentions after the international break, when he’s had a proper opportunity to work with the players on the training pitch.

Speaking during his first pre-match press conference, Parker explained what he liked about the remarkable second-half performance in Cardiff.

“I think a good side would be the one that played in the second half at Cardiff. That was a team I liked – it was an aggressive team, a front-footed team, a team that took risks that was looking to score goals.”

“Certainly, with the players we have, the second-half performance last night was exactly the sort of thing I want to see.”

I find those comments incredibly encouraging, particularly because they recognise something I’ve been saying for some time. West Ham have players who are capable of considerably more than we’ve been seeing, and the second half against Cardiff demonstrated that perfectly.

Whether the shackles were suddenly taken off tactically, I couldn’t possibly say. Parker had barely met his players before the game, and it would be ridiculous to suggest that he’s somehow transformed their tactical understanding during a half time chinwag.

What was abundantly clear, however, was that West Ham played with more belief, freedom and attacking intent than anything we witnessed under Nuno Espírito Santo. There was a willingness to take risks, attack the opposition and get players into dangerous areas, rather than endlessly recycling possession without really threatening anybody.

West Ham will play with more freedom under Parker

Perhaps the clearest demonstration of the difference was Jarrod Bowen, who looked like the best player in the Championship during that second half. The West Ham captain was absolutely unplayable, drifting into central positions, creating chances and having a hand in all three goals.

It was men against boys stuff, really, and I couldn’t help wondering why we haven’t seen more of that from Bowen and his teammates. The quality has always been there, but for whatever reason, we simply haven’t been getting enough out of it.

That doesn’t mean everything was Nuno’s fault, nor does it mean Parker has already discovered the colonels secret recipe. But it does suggest that West Ham have the ability to play with considerably more aggression and purpose than we’ve become accustomed to.

Parker himself was careful to acknowledge that almost every manager would like to play fast, free-flowing attacking football. He also recognised that the reality of management involves making decisions based on the players available and finding a system that suits them.

That’s a sensible observation, and one worth remembering before we start expecting West Ham to produce the Cardiff second half every week. Nevertheless, Parker has already seen evidence of what this squad can do, and he’s made it clear that he wants more of the same.

#2091. Ryan Jack knew Clement was doomed at Rangers as he reveals bad taste in his mouth

A Tuesday night in May and Rangers are hosting Dundee in their last home league game of the season. After seven years, one league title, a Scottish Cup medal and a European final, Ryan Jack is preparing to say farewell to Ibrox.

“I took along all my family that night thinking, ‘it might be my last home game,” he tells Herald Sport.

“I had been to the hotel all day with the team all days and had lunch and a sleep before the bus to Ibrox.

“We got to the stadium pre-match and nobody has said a word to me, so I am thinking I am in the squad and might play…”

Any realistic hope of Rangers winning the league title had extinguished the previous week after a defeat at Parkhead.

Fully recovered from a muscle injury, Jack still had plenty to play for. His contract was up at the end of the season and the Scottish Cup Final against Celtic was just around the corner. Despite injuries corrupting his season he felt sure he still had something to offer.

He had no idea if Philippe Clement felt the same. Whenever he knocked on the manager’s door pinning the Belgian down was like nailing jelly to the wall.

When his name was absent from the squad list for Dundee, he finally had his answer. At 32, he had been around football long enough to sense which way the wind was blowing.

“That was after seven years of graft and putting my life into every day and playing through pain barriers, because that’s what you do.

“That night against Dundee was when I thought that it was not going to work out for Clement at Rangers.

“Because when other people see you treat players who had been there for seven years like that then they say, ‘nah, he’s miles off it.’

“Players are human and it’s like any walk of life. If your boss does that you think, ‘nah, that’s not on.’

Currently a free agent after two years in Turkey, the former Scotland midfielder is taking his time over what comes next. At 34 he wants to play on after the kind of family Christmas he never managed when the festive fixture card piled up one game after another at Aberdeen and Rangers. When he sits down to write some cards to family and friends its safe to assume that the name of the current Norwich City manager won’t be on the list.

“I actually remember guys like Jack Butland, Conor Goldson and James Tavernier and John Lundstram saying to me, ‘that’s an absolute disgrace what the manager has done to you.’

“When that happened the penny dropped that I was definitely going to be leaving for sure.”

For long periods of season 2023/24 Rangers had looked a reasonable bet for the title. Four points adrift of Brendan Rodgers’ Celtic the Ibrox side had the saving grace of two games in hand until they threw the advantage away. They lost the first game in Dingwall to Ross County then failed to find a way through against Dundee in a goalless draw at Dens Park.

By the time they turned around a two goal deficit against the Dark Blues in their final Ibrox home game it was too little, too late. Celtic rattled five goals past Kilmarnock the following night and won their 12th championship in 13 seasons and faith in Clement was draining fast.

An unused substitute as Celtic won the Scottish Cup final with a late Adam Idah goal, Jack delayed his holiday plans to hang back in Glasgow and prepare for a trip to the Euros with Scotland. Despite asking the question - repeatedly - he still had no idea what the future held.

“There were talks ongoing for months and months. It looked like a deal might be happening, then it wasn’t happening.

“You know what it’s like. Managers start having a certain way of communicating with you.

“I went to see him two or three times to say, ‘okay what’s happening here?’

“I wanted to plan for the future and every time it was, ‘oh, we don’t know yet, the club has not made a decision. It’s not my decision.’

“All I wanted was an honest answer. I felt that, when I was fit and well I was still capable of doing a job for sure.

“There were just certain things that made me think my time was coming to an end.”.

As it turned out his last appearance for Rangers came in a 2-2 draw against Benfica in the last 16 of the Europa League in Lisbon in March. A late replacement for Tom Lawrence in the Stadium of Light, a muscle injury ruled him out until he returned to fitness at the end of the season. Even then he didn’t play.

His surprise inclusion in Steve Clarke’s Scotland squad for the Euros in Germany was a reward for his dogged loyalty and performances at international level. He felt none of that payback coming from Philippe Clement.

“I was training for a couple of weeks after the season finished because I wanted to keep ticking over for Euros.

“It was then that he (Clement) phoned me and asked for 10 minutes to speak to me.

“He came in to the training centre and he said that the club had made a decision to go younger and I had suffered a few injuries over my time and that hadn’t helped me with the people above who had doubts.

“He said they wanted to go down a young route and get most of the experienced players out.

“And my comeback to him was, ‘do you think that is the best way to go?’

“A club like Rangers can not just sign a team of players who are 20 or 21 or 22 and expect them to be ready for the expectation and the pressure and the European stage.

“I’ve always felt that, to be successful at Rangers, you need a core who can be around the changing room and lead it. Even if they don’t play every week.

“But he wanted to go young and it didn’t turn out too well for him.”

“That time under Clement left a bad taste - the way he was going about things at the end.”

Jack had known nothing beyond the narrow horizons of Scottish football. Joining Aberdeen’s pro youth system at the age of eight, he rose to become captain of his hometown club. When he took advantage of freedom of contract to sign a three year deal with Rangers in 2017 some took his choice of club badly. His parents’ home address in Aberdeen was posted online accompanied by brainless threats.

“You know what? I grew up a Rangers fan as a young boy and the move wasn’t difficult for me personally.

“I know that the clubs are huge rivals and people take that personally, but I still hold Aberdeen in the highest regard. There was no ill feeling towards the club at all.

“Making the move was always a football decision to go to a new level and play in front of 50,000 people in Europe with a better training facility at the time.

“Off the pitch it brought a lot of stuff and hype media wise, of course it did.

“I’m not going to lie, I felt that pressure when I went back to Pittodrie. Everyone is against you.

“My family stay in the north east and they probably got a bit more of that than I did.

“There were maybe people at Aberdeen who looked at me differently for moving to Rangers, I don’t know.”

One of those who took news of the move to Ibrox badly, ironically, was his Aberdeen manager at the time. One Derek McInnes esq.

“Derek told me that after we played Rangers Pedro Caixinha was in giving it, ‘were going to take your players.’

“Derek had a wee chat with me asking what I was planning. He gave me the captaincy at the club and wanted to build the team around me.

“I loved my time with Derek. Working with him was one of the most enjoyable periods of my career.

“We had a wee bit of a fall out towards the end of the season because he was desperate for me to stay with Aberdeen.

“I wanted to move on and develop my career away from the club, but we are brand new now.”

There was a time, shortly after his own arrival at Ibrox in 2017, when it seemed that McInnes would join him in Glasgow. Jack was told by former Aberdeen teammates that the deal was done until a late u-turn.

McInnes stayed put at Pittodrie, only leaving when he was dismissed in 2021. He found a route to Ibrox eventually - via Kilmarnock and Hearts - while the club which fired him goes through managers like Donald Trump sweats his way through MAGA caps.

Involved with Aberdeen for 17 years Jack thinks the decision to part company with McInnes was a mistake.

“Derek was always made for being at a big club and having that demand on him.

“He knows the league and he knows how to get the job done. And when I look at Aberdeen they have never been able to replace him.

“I think back to the team he assembled when I was there, with Kenny McLean, Adam Rooney, Graeme Shinnie, Jonny Hayes, Niall McGinn, Mark Reynolds, Andy Considine, Shay Logan. Even James Maddison came in on loan for a time.

“We had great characters and we were always finishing second in the league and getting to semi finals and finals every year and yet being captain the whole vibe outside was, ‘we’re not good enough, we cannot compete.’ It was always negative.

“But we were up against Brendan Rodgers and a strong Celtic squad.

“And I don’t think that Aberdeen team that we had will be matched for years to come.

“I don’t know what direction the club wants to go in now or what kind of recruitment they go for.

“It’s mix and match, here, there and everywhere. Managers go from Stephen Glass to Jim Goodwin and Neil Warnock to Stephen Robinson. Yet when I look back at my time with Del it was so settled.”

After two seasons with Turkish club Esenler Erokspor Jack is enjoying some down time back in Scotland. His relationship with McInnes is back on a firm footing and he uses the gym facilities at Auchenhowie to keep fit while he waits for the right offer to get back playing. He is open minded on what comes next.

“I want to play on. I am only 34 and I still feel that I have a bit to give.

“There is no real plan, but I have had a few discussions here and there at a decent enough level with some teams. I want to wait and see what comes up, it needs to be the right place at the right time.

“I am not arrogant about where I play or what I want to do, I have had a good career so far. But I want something that excites me and gives me something to look forward to.”

When the news broke that Jack was using Rangers facilities to keep fit, a post from his former manager Steven Gerrard in Instagram almost broke the internet.

“Put him in the middle,” wrote the England legend. “Proper player.”

“I think that ship has sailed,” says Jack, with a laugh. “I loved my time at the club and have some amazing memories.

“I think Stevie had just seen that I had been training in there and it was a tongue in cheek comment.

“I have said before that the time under Stevie Gerrard was the best football I played in my career.

“Everything he brought when he came in opened my eyes to a new world.”

By  his own admission, he made the most of the talent he had. If anything there were times, under Gerrard, when he pushed his body farther than harder than he should have and it hurt him.

“If I could do more I would do it. If I could train harder I would train harder. If I could run more in a game I did it.

“That’s what the gaffer loved about me. I would never say no.

“I would never say, ‘I’m not training’ or ‘i’m not playing.’

“And that maybe cost me a few injuries over the years.”

Clubs looking for an old head with a ferocious work rate should know that he now feels fit and ready to go. He wants to play while preparing for the next phase.

“It has always fascinated me, managing and having your own team. I want to go down and avenue and see where that leads me…”

#2090. JJ Gabriel future: Man United's stance 'revealed' amid reports of Real Madrid 'agreement'

By Matt Law | 04 Nov 2026 17:12, Last updated: 04 Nov 2026 17:15

Manchester United are reportedly in the dark when it comes to JJ Gabriel's future despite reports that the attacker has agreed a move to Real Madrid.

Widely regarded as one of the best teenagers in world football, JJ Gabriel stunned Man United in September when he told the club that he wanted to leave.

JJ Gabriel made his senior debut for Man United in their pre-season game against Atletico Madrid during the summer, but he is yet to feature for the first team in a competitive match and is now set to leave the 20-time English champions.

The 16-year-old had been due to sign scholarship terms with the Red Devils last month, with a professional contract then expected to follow a year later.

However, JJ Gabriel's representatives told Man United in September that the attacker would not be signing a new contract and wanted to leave.

According to Sky Sports News, Real Madrid have reached a verbal agreement with JJ Gabriel over a move to Bernabeu in January.

JJ Gabriel has a European passport through both of his parents, and a FIFA loophole could see him join Real Madrid in January despite having a deal with Man United's academy until the end of the campaign.

The attacker is currently in Spain maintaining his fitness, and Barcelona have also been heavily linked with a player regarded as one of the best teenagers in world football.

However, various reports have claimed that Real Madrid are closing in on a move.

According to the Manchester Evening News, Man United have had no contact from JJ Gabriel's representatives nor Real Madrid despite the reports.

Man United still hold JJ Gabriel's registration, but the teenager has not been at Carrington since scoring a hat-trick against Sabah in the UEFA Youth League at the start of September.

JJ Gabriel boasts a record of 29 goals and four assists in 32 appearances for Man United Under-18s. while he has scored twice and registered two assists in two appearances for Man United Under-21s in the Premier League 2.

Man United had allegedly initially been hopeful of keeping JJ Gabriel but have since admitted defeat in what is a major blow for the 20-time English champions.

#2089. Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

It was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes showed he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

The one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward quickly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n

Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

You would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA

Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6

It was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

The misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

Decent enough watch for roughly half the game, settled on a shoot-out in which Alex Cairns got nowhere near any of Manchester United’s penalties. Doubt he will lose much sleep over it. Bruno Fernandes grinned broadly when he missed.

Not sure what we can say about stadium safety here but the game has ended prematurely after five kids came on, all of whom got to Bruno Fernandes to take selfies. It was very funny but, equally, plenty on the Manchester United bench were far from happy. Penalties to follow.

Some sealion ball juggling from Mazraoui involving foot, thigh and head, gets him past Justin on the right  but Gnonto heads away his cross.

Two young Man Utd fans run on to the pitch to try to take selfies with Man utd players. They are joined by three more and now another.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

It’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in New Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

While Leeds will have new signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

#2088. Bruno Fernandes admits Michael Carrick was right to drop him

By Naim Beneddra | 04 Nov 2026 17:54

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has admitted that Michael Carrick was justified in dropping him from the starting lineup, while denying reports of a breakdown in his relationship with the under-pressure manager.

The Portugal international made the surprising admission following United's dramatic 3-2 Champions League victory over Roma on Tuesday, which ended a nine-match winless run and provided some much-needed relief at Old Trafford.

Fernandes had been left on the bench for last month's Premier League defeat to Bournemouth, just days after publicly questioning the team's tactical approach following a humiliating 4-1 loss to Como.

His comments prompted speculation that Carrick had punished his captain for speaking out, although the United boss maintained that the decision had been made for footballing reasons.

Now, Fernandes has acknowledged that his own performances warranted the decision, while insisting that the controversy had not affected his confidence in the former England midfielder.

"Carrick was right" ?? Bruno Fernandes gave an open, honest assessment after United's 3-2 win over Roma ?️ https://t.co/QAWDt6VXQr

Speaking to Amazon Prime Video after the Roma victory, Fernandes addressed the circumstances surrounding his absence from the starting lineup against Bournemouth.

The 32-year-old revealed that he understood why Carrick had decided to make a change, even though the timing had led to suggestions of a disciplinary response.

"The manager took a decision of putting me on the bench because I wasn't performing," Fernandes admitted.

"Everyone felt that was a punishment for the words that I had. If it was, it was right."

Those comments represent a notable change in tone from the midfielder, whose public criticism after the Como defeat had intensified scrutiny of Carrick's management.

Fernandes had questioned United's decision not to press their opponents man-to-man and suggested that the players needed to show greater bravery under pressure.

Four days later, he was named among the substitutes for the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth, marking the first time Carrick had dropped him from a Premier League starting lineup.

At the time, the manager insisted that his decision to leave Fernandes out was based purely on footballing considerations.

The captain's latest explanation supports that assessment, although he stopped short of confirming whether his earlier comments had influenced Carrick's thinking.

Fernandes also challenged reports suggesting that he and the manager had needed to resolve a personal disagreement behind the scenes.

He described some of the speculation surrounding their relationship as "lies", rejecting claims that the pair had held talks to clear the air following his controversial interview.

The midfielder was equally clear that being dropped had not diminished his commitment to Carrick or the club.

"It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager," Fernandes insisted, adding that he retained the same confidence in the coaching staff and his teammates.

His response is significant given the uncertainty surrounding Carrick's position and the questions that have been raised about the mood within United's dressing room.

Rather than portraying his omission as an injustice, Fernandes has publicly accepted responsibility for his performances and acknowledged the manager's authority to make difficult selection decisions.

Fernandes also responded to suggestions that United's remarkable recovery against Roma might have saved Carrick from dismissal.

The Red Devils had entered Tuesday's encounter without a victory in nine matches across all competitions, having slipped to 17th in the Premier League.

Their situation appeared to deteriorate further when Matias Soule and Donyell Malen gave Roma a two-goal advantage in the opening stages at Old Trafford.

However, Fernandes converted a retaken penalty in the second half before Matheus Cunha scored twice late on to complete the comeback.

Asked afterwards whether the players had rescued their manager's job, the United captain rejected that interpretation.

"We don't need to save anyone's job," Fernandes declared.

He explained that the victory had been necessary for the entire club after a prolonged period of poor results, rather than solely for Carrick's personal circumstances.

The Portuguese also acknowledged the frustration felt by supporters, who have watched United struggle to reproduce the standards associated with the club's most successful years.

Carrick adopted a similarly measured approach in his post-match comments, describing the victory as an important moment for the club without suggesting that one result had resolved its problems.

United's next test comes against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday, November 8, when they will attempt to secure consecutive victories for the first time in several weeks.

Fernandes has already returned to Carrick's starting lineup, featuring against Chelsea before playing a decisive role in the European comeback.

His latest comments may help dispel some of the speculation surrounding his relationship with the manager. Whether United can build on Tuesday's result will provide a more meaningful indication of Carrick's prospects of remaining in charge.

#2087. Martin O'Neill issues fresh Joel van den Berg verdict after Celtic B appearance

Martin O'Neill says he'll demand 'a lot more' of Joel van den Berg after watching the midfielder in action for Celtic B against Ross County on Tuesday evening.

O'Neill travelled to Dingwall with coaches Mark Fotheringham and Stephen McManus for the Scottish Challenge Cup tie.

Along with Van den Berg, first-team duo Shim Mheuka and Landon Emenalo featured from the start as Celtic B lost 2-0.

The Netherlands youth international, signed from PSV Eindhoven for £3.5 million during the summer transfer window, completed 72 minutes.

"He's just back from injury. I thought his training sessions had been very, very good," O'Neill said of Van den Berg. "And I'm going to demand a lot more of him."

O'Neill hasn't shied away from giving youth a chance since returning as Celtic manager last year.

Colby Donovan has emerged as a first-team regular during his second and third tenures, with numerous youngsters involved in pre-season a few months back.

The 74-year-old even spoke to the players after Tuesday's defeat.

"That was wildly important for me to go up to that game [in Dingwall], really," O'Neill added. "Because there are two things to it.

"Young boys want to see the manager there. And I do go. I went to a lot of the B team games last year as well down at Barrowfield. I feel that that's my job at the end of the day.

"And while I might not be around, seriously, to see the likes of Liam Kennedy or people like this to mature and become [first-team players], you would take at least half an ounce of satisfaction that you saw them and that you were at least saying something to them that might help them get out of it.

"The new manager coming in might just give totally different advice. I don't know. But I think that my advice to young players, this is not boastful, I promise you, I think it's the right way.

"I give you an instance which I said to the team the other night. They were beaten by a very, very strong, and committed Ross County team.

"But it was important for me to see, first of all, the young Chelsea lads playing, then Joel [van den Berg] coming back from injury, seeing what he's capable of doing.

"But my things will not change in this game. Whatever changes they make to the game, you have the defenders to be able to defend. You've got full-backs whose first job is to think about stopping crosses from coming in. And then when they want to come and join in and be something.

"You need your attacking midfield players on the half-turn, making something happen. Don't be playing it back all day long. I could do that.

"You need your centre forwards to get hold of the ball – that's something that Brian Clough preached. He didn’t care whether the centre forwards scored the goals, as long as they held the ball up and played people into the game.

"You also need wingers to take people on. Those things do not change. And it doesn't matter about tactics. It doesn't matter about jumping. It doesn't matter about man for man. It doesn't matter about all of these things. It's what you do.

"I've seen it a thousand times, players with terrific ability when they're 17, 18, being given the wrong information and not realising their potential because they didn't have it."

#2086. Famalicao vs Arouca - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 04 Nov 2026 18:51

Seaching for their first home victory this season, Famalicao welcome an in-form Arouca side to the Estadio Municipal 22 de Junho on Friday night.

The hosts sit 11th in the Primeira Liga table, three points above the relegation zone, while the visitors occupy fifth place, ahead of sixth-placed Academico de Viseu on goal difference.

Famalicao have struggled to reproduce the form that earned them a club-best fifth-place finish last season, with the departures of former boss Hugo Oliveira, Ibrahima Ba and Gustavo Sa contributing to a difficult start to the new campaign.

Carlos Carvalhal, who took over in the summer, was dismissed in October following a shock Taca de Portugal defeat to third-tier Paredes, leaving 46-year-old assistant coach Ricardo Silva in charge on an interim basis.

Although Silva made an impressive start, securing a 4-0 away victory over Rio Ave before edging Braga on penalties in the Taca da Liga quarter-finals, the Vila Nova outfit were brought back down to earth by the same Minho rivals at the weekend, suffering a 3-0 league defeat.

That result leaves Famalicao with just two wins from their opening 10 Primeira Liga fixtures this season (D4, L4), while they have scored 14 goals and conceded the same number, highlighting the need for greater efficiency at both ends of the pitch.

The Vila Nova outfit have also struggled at the Estadio Municipal 22 de Junho this term, with Fama among three sides in the division yet to record a home victory, having collected just two points from four outings on their own turf, the most recent of which was a 4-1 defeat to Alverca.

Arouca, on the other hand, arrive in considerably better shape compared to the hosts, having enjoyed an impressive start under Vitor Severino, who took charge in October following Vasco Seabra's departure for Rio Ave.

Although the Wolves had enjoyed an encouraging campaign under Seabra, Severino inherited a side that had gone three matches without a win but has since guided them to four consecutive victories across the league and Taca de Portugal.

An extra-time cup victory over Belenenses came between three successive 1-0 league wins against Estrela Amadora, Alverca and Nacional, leaving Arouca with 13 goals scored and seven conceded in their opening 10 Primeira Liga matches, as well as a joint-league-high six clean sheets.

The Wolves have also been resilient on their travels, with their only defeat in five league trips this season coming against defending champions Porto, while two victories and two draws have given them eight points and made them the division's eighth-best away side.

However, Arouca have struggled in recent meetings with Famalicao, going winless in their last four competitive encounters and losing two of their previous three league visits to Vila Nova, while failing to score during that period.

Famalicao will be without Rodrigo Pinheiro, who is suspended after being sent off during last weekend's league defeat to Braga.

Georgios Koutsias is expected to lead the attack after scoring five league goals this season, while Sorriso and Romeo Beney could provide support from the flanks, with Oscar Aranda another option in the wide areas.

Arouca have a considerably cleaner bill of health, with Miguel Puche their only notable absentee as he continues his recovery from an anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Gabriel Rukavina is available again after serving a one-match suspension following his dismissal against Alverca, although the midfielder is yet to start a league game since joining from Rijeka in the summer.

Ivan Barbero should lead the line as he looks to add to his five league goals this season, while Nais Djouahra is expected to feature prominently after registering five assists in the competition.

Famalicao's home struggles and the uncertainty surrounding their interim management make it difficult to back them against an Arouca side that has found its rhythm and been particularly solid defensively, so a narrow away victory looks likely.

Erling Haaland will captain Manchester City in tonight’s Champions League clash against RB Leipzig at the Red Bull Arena.

#2083. Scotland boss hails 'buy-in' as senior trio embrace Under-21 drop

Scotland Under-21s head coach Tony Docherty is delighted with the buy-in from the three players who have dropped down from the senior squad.

Colby Donovan, Lennon Miller and James Wilson have all been included in a new-look Scotland Under-21 squad for friendlies against Ukraine and United States in Spain this month.

The three players were all in Sebastian Pocogonoli’s first full Scotland squad and join Tyler Fletcher, who went to the World Cup before joining Docherty’s group in September.

“I’m really, really delighted with the introduction of the ones that have had that A squad experience, and they’re really the drivers,” Docherty said. “They become your leadership group that drives standards, create that mentality, get that identity.

“You’ve seen that in the last camp when I was out at the A squad camp and I returned with James and Findlay (Curtis), and then Findlay goes back up again as a result of his performance.

“Lennon and Colby Donovan, I’ve had dialogue with both of them quite a bit over the last couple of days, just to outline what their pathway is.

“If they’re not going to be getting minutes for this camp with the A squad, it’s important they come in to my squad and it will be a mirror image in terms of structure, fundamentals. And they just come in and get an opportunity to get game time.

“So, really pleased that Lennon, Colby and you can include Fletch, James in that, they don’t just come to the 21s, they really participate.

“I had a particularly long conversation with Lennon. You’ve seen the example, the last camp there with Barney Stewart. He comes in, he scores three goals, he’s in a good place when he gets back, gets into West Brom’s first team, scores a couple of goals, they win a couple of games.

“I had a good conversation with Colby and he just wants to play. So it’s important that we’ve got the buy-in. It’s not us telling Colby, ‘you’re playing with the 21s’, it’s him in dialogue with us saying, ‘I want to do that, I want to play and I want to impress’.

“And that’s very much where we are now, and that’s a relationship I think is really healthy.”

St Mirren striker Eseosa Sule has been called up as Docherty prepares for a new European qualifying campaign after 16 of the 27 players from his first squad went beyond the age level.

Rangers youth player Kyle Glasgow drops to the Scotland Under-19 squad for three European qualifying games. The 16-year-old on-loan Alloa player joins elder brother Euan Glasgow, who plays for Edinburgh City on loan from Hearts.

#2082. Report: Liverpool increasingly likely to sanction January exit for player in ‘agonising’ situation

One Liverpool player seems increasingly likely to leave Anfield in January as his situation on Merseyside becomes ‘increasingly agonising’.

Having struggled for starts in two seasons under Arne Slot, Federico Chiesa would no doubt have been hoping that a change of head coach might’ve provided the springboard towards an increase in game-time.

Instead, the 29-year-old’s standing at LFC has diminished even further, having played just two minutes under Andoni Iraola so far despite recovering from a back injury almost a month ago.

According to Dean Jones for Flashscore, a January exit from Liverpool for the forward seems ‘increasingly possible’, and a return to his native Italy ‘could provide an attractive solution’ for both player and club.

Lazio, Inter Milan and Roma have been touted as clubs who ‘could explore the possibility’ of bringing Chiesa back to Serie A after he left Juventus for the Reds in 2024, although any such move would depend on what kind of deal the Merseysiders are prepared to consider.

The report adds that the 29-year-old’s situation ‘is becoming increasingly agonising’ as he continues to struggle for game-time at Anfield.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

That Chiesa didn’t even make the substitutes’ bench against Arsenal on Sunday despite being fit and available is a damning indictment of where he stands in the pecking order.

The additions of Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola over the summer added further competition for places in the forward line, and the form of Lewis Koumas has seen him leap ahead of the Italian in the queue.

Iraola had six forwards either as starters or substitutes at the weekend, and he still has Hugo Ekitike to return from injury, so Chiesa is effectively our eighth-choice attacker.

His status at Liverpool was summed up a few weeks ago by Roy Keane’s throwaway comment of ‘Is he still there?‘ when the 29-year-old’s name was mentioned on the Stick To Football podcast, and the situation hasn’t gotten any better for our number 14 in the meantime.

Barring a substantial injury crisis in the forward line (heaven forbid), it’s hard to see the Italian getting much of a look-in at Anfield any time soon, and it’s looking increasingly likely that he could be allowed to leave for his homeland in January.

It’d be a shame of his time with the Reds petered out to that extent, but Chiesa would depart as a genuine cult hero among Kopites for what he has contributed over the past two-and-a-bit years.

#2080. Joao Neves rules out Premier League move in PSG pledge

By Naim Beneddra | 04 Nov 2026 18:52

Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Joao Neves has delivered a clear message about his future, revealing that he has no ambition to play in the Premier League or La Liga despite previously attracting interest from some of Europe's biggest clubs.

The 22-year-old Portugal international has established himself as a key figure in Luis Enrique's side since arriving from Benfica in 2024, helping the French champions secure back-to-back Champions League titles.

However, Neves has now gone a step further than simply expressing his satisfaction with life in Paris, revealing that he would like to spend the remainder of his playing career at the Parc des Princes.

His comments come shortly after signing a new contract until June 2031 and ahead of PSG's continued pursuit of a third successive European crown.

The midfielder also underlined his importance on the pitch on Tuesday evening, opening the scoring and providing an assist in PSG's emphatic 6-0 Champions League victory away to Villarreal.

Speaking in an interview with French broadcaster CANAL+, Neves made it clear that moving to either England or Spain is not among his career objectives.

"I don't have the objective of going to Spain or England," the former Benfica youngster explained.

"I have an objective, and it is to feel good in my life and to win here. Joao wants to stay here his whole career."

The declaration is particularly significant given Neves's age and the transfer speculation that has surrounded him since his emergence in Portuguese football.

Manchester United were among the clubs linked with the midfielder before his move to PSG, while Manchester City were subsequently credited with an interest in bringing him to the Etihad Stadium.

In September 2025, reports suggested that City were considering an offer worth approximately £105m for Neves, although PSG were understood to be unwilling to entertain his departure.

That speculation never developed into a confirmed transfer agreement, and there is no indication that either Manchester club is currently negotiating for his signature.

Nevertheless, Neves's latest comments suggest that even the prospect of playing in England's top flight holds little appeal to him at present.

His position is supported by his recent contractual commitment.

In September, PSG announced a series of extensions involving several important members of Luis Enrique's squad, including Neves, Willian Pacho, Lucas Beraldo, Senny Mayulu and Fabian Ruiz.

The Portuguese midfielder's agreement now runs until the summer of 2031, giving the French champions considerable security over his future.

While such a contract does not rule out a transfer later in his career, Neves has made his personal preference unusually clear.

For Premier League clubs hoping to attract one of Europe's most accomplished young midfielders, his comments provide little encouragement.

Neves's commitment to PSG is closely connected to the success he has experienced since leaving Benfica.

The Portugal international has developed into an integral part of Luis Enrique's midfield alongside compatriot Vitinha, combining an ability to regain possession with the technical quality required to operate in tight spaces.

His contribution has been particularly important to PSG's recent European dominance.

Since his arrival in 2024, the French club have won two consecutive Champions League titles, establishing themselves among the continent's leading teams.

Neves has also demonstrated that his role extends beyond winning possession and maintaining control in midfield.

Against Villarreal on Tuesday, he opened the scoring after nine minutes, reacting quickly inside the penalty area following a corner.

He later supplied the assist for David Boly's goal as PSG completed their record-breaking away victory in the Champions League.

The result maintained the defending champions' perfect record in this season's league phase, with four victories from their opening four matches.

Despite that impressive start, Neves believes maintaining the standards established over the previous two seasons will present a considerable challenge.

"It's the mentality," he explained when discussing PSG's continued ambition.

"You have two Champions Leagues, but you keep making the necessary efforts. Maintaining that quality is even harder than winning two Champions Leagues."

The midfielder also identified a specific objective for the current European campaign.

"We want to try to finish in the top eight, something we haven't managed in the last two seasons."

That target reflects PSG's determination to avoid the additional knockout-round play-offs and secure direct qualification for the last 16.

Neves's performances against Villarreal offered another illustration of why Luis Enrique considers him central to those ambitions.

And while his contract already ties him to Paris for several more years, his latest declaration suggests that he sees no need to leave the French capital to fulfil his remaining ambitions in football.

Virgil van Dijk has advised Liverpool to forget about what their Premier League rivals are doing and concentrate on themselves, following the defeat to Arsenal at the weekend.

It was a second home defeat in the space of a month for LFC, who were also beaten on their own patch by second-placed Manchester City, and the veteran Dutch defender acknowledged that his team are in a transitional phase after changing head coach over the summer.

Speaking to reporters after the defeat to Arsenal, Van Dijk proclaimed (via Liverpool Echo): “We have to just focus on ourselves.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Nobody realistically expected Liverpool to challenge for the title at the start of the season, so it wouldn’t be a failure if the Reds aren’t in contention for the trophy by the time April rolls around.

The objective for this campaign was to finish closer to the summit and show discernible improvement on a wretched 2025/26, and recent performances suggest that Iraola is capable of delivering in that regard.

His team are currently on course to end the season with 63 points (just three more than last term), but if they improve on a home record of just one win from five league games so far, they should be able to nudge that projected total into the 70s.

Liverpool competed admirably with Arsenal and Man City (up until the harsh red card for Ryan Gravenberch) but weren’t as clinical as the top two in those games. With more ruthlessness in attack, the Reds seem capable of at least closing that gap.

Van Dijk is correct – the goal for this season isn’t to compete for the title, but to qualify for the Champions League with relative comfort and lay the foundations for further improvement in 2027/28.

There’s still plenty of room for improvement, but at least there are signs of this campaign being much more convincing than 2025/26 had been.

#2076. Frenkie De Jong hits back at critics and sends Hansi Flick message

By Naim Beneddra | 04 Nov 2026 19:44

Barcelona midfielder Frenkie de Jong has expressed his frustration at the constant speculation surrounding him, while making it clear that he wants to reclaim a regular starting place under Hansi Flick.

The Netherlands international spoke out after reaching 300 appearances for the Catalan giants during Tuesday's 3-0 Champions League victory over Aston Villa, having recently returned from a lengthy injury absence.

De Jong believes that his performances, fitness and future attract considerably more scrutiny than those of his teammates, particularly when he is unavailable for selection.

However, the 29-year-old also delivered an encouraging update on his physical condition, insisting that his knee is no longer causing problems and that he is ready to compete for a more prominent role.

His comments arrive at an important moment for Flick, with Barcelona preparing to face Atletico Madrid this weekend and uncertainty emerging over the availability of fellow midfielder Rodri.

Speaking to reporters following the victory over Aston Villa, De Jong acknowledged that the speculation surrounding him had become a recurring source of frustration.

"There is always a bit of noise around me, especially when I'm not there," the midfielder said, as quoted by Mundo Deportivo.

"For some reason, in the summer when there is no football, or when I'm injured..."

De Jong went on to suggest that he receives more attention than other members of the Barcelona squad, although he accepted that this might partly reflect his personal perception.

"I feel that there is always more noise around me than around others. But perhaps that's just my impression when people talk about me. These are things I don't have much control over."

The Dutchman's remarks follow several months of questions about his fitness and position at Camp Nou.

De Jong sustained a knee ligament injury while representing the Netherlands at the 2026 World Cup, leaving him unavailable for the opening weeks of Barcelona's campaign.

During his recovery, he also addressed reports concerning his relationship with Flick and the club's hierarchy, rejecting suggestions that he had fallen out with the German coach.

His latest comments suggest that the scrutiny remains a sensitive subject, even after his return to competitive action.

Nevertheless, De Jong was keen to emphasise that his physical condition has improved considerably.

"I feel very good, very strong, with a lot of desire and motivation," he explained.

"My knee isn't bothering me. What's happened has happened."

The midfielder made his first appearance of the season as a substitute against Real Madrid on October 25, before starting Barcelona's emphatic 6-1 league victory over Alaves six days later.

Flick deployed him in central defence against Alaves, illustrating the versatility that has allowed the former Ajax player to operate in several positions during his Barcelona career.

Tuesday's Champions League encounter brought another significant moment, as De Jong replaced Pedri in the 70th minute to make his 300th competitive appearance for the club.

He was subsequently presented with a commemorative shirt by his teammates.

Having already surpassed Philip Cocu and Ronald Koeman, De Jong holds the record for the most competitive appearances by a Dutch player in Barcelona's history.

Despite his willingness to help in defence, De Jong made no secret of his preferred position or his desire to return to the starting lineup.

"I feel more comfortable in midfield, but I will help the team wherever it needs me," he said.

Asked whether he hoped to start against Atletico Madrid on Sunday, the Dutch international acknowledged that his recent injury would influence Flick's decision.

"I would like to start matches, but we have to take into account that I've been out for a long time, and that depends on the coaching staff."

His comments are particularly relevant following Rodri's withdrawal at half time against Aston Villa.

The former Manchester City midfielder complained of muscular discomfort during Tuesday's encounter, prompting Flick to introduce Marc Bernal for the second half.

Barcelona have since confirmed a minor hamstring injury, leaving Rodri's availability for the trip to Atletico in doubt.

Flick has already suggested that Bernal could be considered as a replacement, while also pointing out that De Jong has only recently returned from injury.

That leaves the Barcelona manager with a decision to make over his midfield combination, particularly given the demands of facing one of La Liga's strongest opponents away from home.

De Jong's ability to operate alongside Pedri, provide defensive cover or contribute further forward gives Flick another option, but his limited minutes this season remain a consideration.

The Dutchman has repeatedly expressed his commitment to Barcelona, having signed a contract extension until June 2029.

His immediate priority, however, is considerably more straightforward: putting his injury problems behind him and earning a place in the team through his performances.

After reaching 300 appearances, De Jong is determined that his next chapter at Barcelona should be defined by what he contributes on the pitch rather than the speculation surrounding him.

#2075. Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn

An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.

Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

The visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box. Jimenez and his wife marked his return to Molineux by giving 5,000 fans black scarves emblazoned with the words ‘Si Senor’ - a nod to his song - and Jimenez did not disappoint as he rifled in his penalty.

LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU

Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

Peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

“We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

“We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”

Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

“Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

"A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq

Blackburn drew level through an unlikely source just nine minutes later as McLoughlin headed in his first-ever goal in English football in more than 150 games when he met Ryoya Morishita’s cross from the right at the near post.

The home side had chances to retake the lead before the break as Lopez curled a shot narrowly over the top from 20-yards while Kieran Trippier teed up Mateus Mane for a chance as the teenager found the top of the net from distance.

Blackburn turned the game on its head minutes after the break as Gudjohnsen turned home Afolayan’s deflected ball in from the right from close range to stun Molineux into silence.

"It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK

Peixoto introduced Jimenez from the bench on the hour mark but even the Mexican could not lift Wolves with Blackburn comfortable for long periods as frustration grew in the stands.

However, Alebiosu handled Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross from the left in injury time and the referee awarded a spot kick which allowed Jimenez to mark his Wolves return with an equaliser from 12-yards as he sent Balazs Toth the wrong way.
