#2017. Celtic support group issues 'have a look' call over Dermot Desmond's stake

Celtic support group Celtic Supporters Limited has called for the Takeover Panel to examine issues surrounding Dermot Desmond’s shareholding in the club.

The group wants the body to look at the circumstances around Desmond’s stake and whether questions over influence and control merit further examination.

Speaking on the Let Me Be Frank podcast, Celtic Supporters Limited chairman Duncan Smillie stressed the support group was not accusing Desmond of wrongdoing, but believes there are grounds for the Takeover Panel to look at the matter.

Smillie said: “If a single shareholder takes their stake in a company above 30 per cent... they are obliged to make an offer for all the shares in a company. That happened to Dave King at Rangers.

“Dermot, in 2005... bought his shares pretty much at a third of the market price... took his shareholding up to 34 per cent or 35 per cent. That then triggers the Takeover Panel. One of the main things you have to guarantee is that you will not try to exert control on that club.

“We at CSL are not making an accusation; we’re not saying he’s done something he shouldn’t have done.

“All we’re asking the Takeover Panel is to have a look at this, because there’s some anecdotal and some real evidence that he has exerted control over the club.”

The intervention comes as Celtic Supporters Limited prepares to raise wider concerns over the club’s shareholding structure and the number of supporters who have become disconnected from their shares.

CSL director Brian McLaughlin said: “There are 37,000 shareholders in Celtic PLC, and many of them have become disconnected from their shares over the years... died, moved house, whatever it may be.

Celtic know they 'need strengthening' as January transfer intel emerges

WATCH: Ex-Celtic star nets first goal in new manager’s dramatic debut

Celtic handed major injury boost as key star returns to training

“They were given a piece of paper in 1994. That piece of paper could be anywhere, in the loft, in the bin, you know.

“Our AGM [resolution] is quite simply tasking Celtic... to go to the company that is the registrar of the shareholding... and say: reunite all our shareholders with their shares. Put the power that they’ve got back in their hands.”

The support group believes reconnecting shareholders with their stakes is important to restoring the balance between supporter and corporate ownership.

McLaughlin added: “When Fergus [McCann] sold his shares, it was always about having a balance between the fan shareholding and the corporate shareholding.

“And that balance is gone. It's corporate shareholding now. Between Desmond and Lindsell Train, they're well above 50 per cent.”

Smillie believes the number of disconnected shareholders can also affect how influential a major shareholder is in practical terms.

He said: “When you’ve got 100 per cent of your shares out there, and you’re a principal shareholder like Dermot Desmond is... let’s say you’ve got 35 per cent for argument's sake. If you’ve got 35 per cent of 100 per cent, that’s a genuine 35 per cent.

“But if there’s a whole chunk of those missing and you actually have 35 per cent of 80 per cent or 85 per cent, you start to have an even more dominant position.

“So it’s maybe not in his personal interest... I think the club like that everybody’s detached.”

Celtic Supporters Limited will now seek to put the share-register issue firmly on the agenda ahead of Celtic’s upcoming AGM.

#2011. Erling Haaland cuts off his trademark blond hair

Erling Haaland has unveiled a dramatic new look after cutting off his trademark blond locks.

The Manchester City striker revealed his new buzzcut hairstyle on Sunday morning ahead of his side’s Premier League opener at home to Bournemouth later in the day.

Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.

Pep Guardiola's reaction to Erling Haaland's new haircut. 😭😂📲 Watch: https://t.co/4KvxC9e5mx pic.twitter.com/QQBCKKpGkP

Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.

Haaland removed his hairband during a 4-1 win over Arsenal in 2023 on a raucous night at the Etihad as City beat their title rivals to move one step closer to winning the league. There will be no need for one now, though, with a close-cut look to mark a new campaign.

It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

Maresca added: “Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do. It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.

“But we need to adapt and we don’t want to keep players here that don’t want to stay.

“The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.

“It’s normal, I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different.”

#2010. Chelsea news: three positives and two disappointments... verdict on five players sent to Strasbourg

By Axel Clody | 05 Nov 2026 07:02

Very active in the last summer transfer window, Strasbourg signed five players from Chelsea. A few weeks after their arrival in Alsace, what is the verdict on their first steps with the club?

Revived by a home thrashing of Auxerre (5-1) after four consecutive defeats, Strasbourg have had a stop-start opening to the season.

Probably not helped by too big a squad overhaul in the last summer window, with close to £85m (€100m) spent and 17 signings registered, the Alsace club are suffering the full effect of a transfer mistake recently highlighted by Ismael Doukoure: a sizeable quota of foreign players and not a single signing with any Ligue 1 experience.

Among the summer arrivals, Hugo Oliveira’s side signed five players from Chelsea, the club with which Strasbourg share the same owner, BlueCo, in a collaboration designed to make transactions between the two sides easier.

They are Brazilian forward Deivid Washington, who cost £13.6m (€16m), English attacking midfielder Omari Kellyman, who cost £5.1m (€6m), Danish goalkeeper Filip Jorgensen on loan, Portuguese defensive midfielder Dario Essugo on loan and Swedish right-back Genesis Antwi on loan. Five players with radically different playing time and performances since the start of the 2026-27 season.

A few months after their arrival in France, what verdict can be drawn? Three positives and two disappointments stand out.

On the positive side, Dario Essugo has made four starts in seven appearances, with two goals and one assist. In terms of presence on the pitch, Filip Jorgensen outstrips the competition with nine starts in nine matches and a status strengthened by wearing the captain’s armband in three games. Although he has not yet kept a clean sheet, he has made 32 saves.

Genesis Antwi, for his part, has started eight times, with Hugo Oliveira only leaving him on the bench against Auxerre. The 19-year-old has just been rewarded for his good performances with a first call-up to Graham Potter’s Sweden squad for the upcoming international break and the Nations League matches against Bosnia-Herzegovina and Poland.

For the two other Chelsea recruits, however, the verdict is not very impressive. Deivid Washington, Strasbourg’s second most expensive signing of summer 2026, has so far been a flop: the Brazilian has still not played a single minute.

Finally, Omari Kellyman has only one appearance, for just six minutes, in a 3-0 defeat to Rennes on 25 October. In other words, the pile-up of players in Strasbourg’s squad has not stopped some from standing out while others remain on the sidelines. It is one way of weighing up the pros and cons of the club’s huge summer 2026 recruitment drive.

After the victory in the derby against Inter, AC Milan have two more games before the November break. However, the mercato never stop.

According to Gianluca Di Marzio, the official announcement of Markus Krösche’s arrival as the new Head of Football is expected on December 1st. Amorim will meet with the German to explain the squad’s needs ahead of the January window, with Gerry Cardinale insisting the club will be ‘active’.

The Rossoneri will therefore return to their search for a defender, especially considering that in the final days of the transfer window they made an attempt for Sporting CP’s Gonçalo Inácio.

The Portuguese club rejected Milan’s offer, attempting to get a better price while also not having time to replace him. Milan are expected try again for Inacio, who played 186 matches under Amorim at Sporting between 2020 and 2024.

The Amorim-Krösche discussion will inevitably also bring up the question of the striker, more specifically the fate of Francesco Camarda. He has only five appearances and 96 minutes of action, so a loan for the second half of the season is not ruled out.

It will therefore be necessary to decide what kind of player to pair with Gonçalo Ramos. The former PSG player continues to play a key role for the team, with a spirit of sacrifice that drives him to run a lot, so Amorim and Krösche will have to factor that into their strategy.

#2007. Mikel Arteta admits Arsenal star 'needed' a good performance as star grabs chance

Mikel Arteta admitted Viktor Gyokeres “needed” a good performance after he starred in the 2-1 Champions League win at Slavia Prague.

Sweden striker Gyokeres made one goal and scored the other in one of his best displays since joining the Gunners in July 2025.

The 28-year-old has played second fiddle to Kai Havertz this season and had scored only one goal before Wednesday night, in the Carabao Cup penalty shoot-out defeat at Fleetwood last month.

But against Slavia, Gyokeres laid on the opener for Noni Madueke before scoring a stylish second on a hugely encouraging evening in the Czech capital.

Read more: This can't go on at Celtic – or can it? O'Neill fears and the McGregor dilemma

“I thought he was really good,” Gunners boss Arteta told reporters. “It was a game we believed would be really good for him, for the demands the opponent puts in and the spaces he could use.

“He’s done it really well, not just for the assist and the goal, but he was really connected to the team. It’s really great news for him, because he really needed that performance.

“He did that really well, understood really well when to appear, when to threaten, because they leave people, they follow man-to-man in the midfield and leave spaces there.

“So when I said he was really connected to the team, that was another example. I thought he had a great performance alongside the goal and assist.

“I’d imagine every player wants to play every game, and Viktor is no different.

“The players need to impact the game like he has done when they get the opportunity, to show the level they can produce. It’s really positive for the team.”

Despite his lack of minutes on the pitch, Gyokeres has now contributed to five goals in his last five matches.

“I feel very good,” he told Arsenal’s website. “Obviously, I’m happy with the win and to contribute to the two goals.”

Premier League leaders Arsenal are up to third in the Champions League table despite a wobble in the second half, when Wiktor Nowak’s 90th-minute goal left them clinging on throughout stoppage time.

“A good feeling in the first half – and then obviously in the second half, with how that went, maybe the feeling isn’t as good. But overall, if you look at the first half, it’s a good feeling,” added Gyokeres.

“It’s my job as a striker and of course I want to contribute every game when I’m on the pitch and want to be involved as much as I can in attacks.

“So far we’ve had a good run in the Champions League and in the league as well.

“At the stage we’re in right now, we’re in a good spot, but I think we’re all clear on what we can improve and what we need to do to take the next step.”

#2004. Barcelona: Raphinha to extend contract until 2030, three factors behind new deal

By Axel Clody | 05 Nov 2026 07:10

There could not be a better time for Raphinha to have his contract renewed by Barcelona. On Thursday, Barcelona will extend the deal of the Brazilian, who is the team’s current captain, until mid-2030, according to Trivela.

As well as being handed the captain’s armband this season, the Brazil international forward is arguably the best player in the world since the competitions began in August. Playing as a centre-forward, he has become a goal machine: 19 in only 13 matches in 2026-27.

It is a revolution the forward has experienced at the Catalan club since 2024. Signed in 2022, he was criticised and even questioned his future at the club, wavering over proposals from Saudi football.

The turning point came with the arrival of Hansi Flick, who convinced him to stay and turned him into one of the best players in the world, first on the left wing. In 2024-25, the German manager’s first year, he set career records for goals (34) and assists (22). After a poorer last year because of injuries, he has returned in full force this season.

His good form was one of the reasons for the renewal, as Trivela learned from an anonymous source who had contact with the negotiations. But it is not the only factor.

Raphinha and his staff understood that extending the contract was the best path given the moment he is experiencing and, in particular, because he is treated by the manager and the club as an important player. This is evident in every word Flick says about the Brazilian, always showering him with praise.

‘He is playing at a spectacular level. His strengths and characteristics fit our style perfectly. He always finds spaces to attack, and we also have players who can provide the final pass. He is very focused, he is our captain and he is showing his quality, which is important for us,’ Flick said after the 6-1 win over Alaves last weekend.

The captaincy mentioned by the manager was his own choice to reward the leadership of the number 11. Raphinha has always been a reference for younger players, which built trust in the dressing room, according to Trivela.

Having a foreigner as captain of one of the biggest clubs in the world is a weighty matter, but it came naturally. The Brazilian has won over the fans and created an identification that also made a difference in the renewal. For that reason there were no obstacles and the negotiation went smoothly for both sides.

When the new contract ends, Raphinha will be 33.

He is already the fourth Brazilian with the most goals for the club, with 94, level with Ronaldinho and behind only Neymar (105) and Rivaldo (130). In the overall ranking he is already in the top 25. In the Champions League, he has just equalled Robert Lewandowski, both with 23 goals, and is surpassed only by Luis Suarez and Lionel Messi.

He is a player who is increasingly becoming a Barcelona idol and, if he maintains his individual level and adds collective trophies, could finish the season as the best in the world.

#2003. Date and time of Celtic AGM revealed as 18 resolutions on table

Celtic have announced the date of the club's AGM for 2026.

The annual general meeting will take place on Tuesday, December 1. It will be held at Celtic Park with a start time of 12pm. The notice for the plans for the AGM is available on the club website.

The AGM agenda makes clear that there will be 18 resolutions.

The resolutions to be considered are as follows:

13.That, pursuant to section 551 of the Companies Act 2006 and Article 6 of the Company'sarticles of association ("Articles"), the directors be and are generally and unconditionally

This authority is in substitution for all existing authorities under section 551 of the Companies Act 2006 which authorities, to the extent unused at the date of this resolution, are revoked with immediate effect.

14. That, subject to the passing of Resolution 13 and pursuant to section 570 of the Companies Act 2006 (and Article 6 of the Articles), the directors be and are generally empowered to allot equity securities (within the meaning of section 560 of the Companies Act 2006) for cash pursuant to the authority conferred by Resolution 13 as if section 561(1) of the Companies Act 2006 did not apply to any such allotment, provided that this power shall be limited to:

14.1 the allotment of equity securities in connection with an offer (whether by way of a rights issue, open offer or otherwise):

14.1.1 to holders of ordinary shares (within the meaning of section 560(1) of the Companies Act 2006) in the capital of the Company in proportion (as nearly as practicable) to the respective numbers of ordinary shares held by them; and

14.1.2 to holders of other equity securities in the capital of the Company, as required by the rights of those securities, or subject to such rights, as the directors otherwise consider necessary,

but subject to such exclusions or other arrangements as the directors may deem necessary or expedient in relation to treasury shares, record dates, fractional entitlements or any legal or practical problems under the laws of any territory or the requirements of any regulatory body or stock exchange;

14.2 the allotment of equity securities in place of a cash dividend pursuant to any authority conferred upon the directors in accordance with and pursuant to Article 40.8 of the Articles; and

14.3 the allotment of equity securities otherwise than pursuant to sub-paragraphs 14.1 and 14.2 above, up to an aggregate nominal amount of £47,577.62;

and (unless previously revoked, varied or renewed) this power shall expire on the earlier of 1 March 2028 and the conclusion of the next annual general meeting of the Company after the passing of this resolution, save that the Company may make an offer or agreement before the expiry of this power which would or might require equity securities to be allotted for cash after such expiry and the directors may allot equity securities pursuant to any such offer or agreement as if this power had not expired.

This power is in substitution for all existing powers under section 570 of the Companies Act 2006 which powers, to the extent unused at the date of this resolution, are revoked with immediate effect.

Resolutions 15, 16, 17 and 18 are ordinary resolutions, requisitioned on behalf of members of the Company in accordance with section 338 of the Companies Act 2006 and are not proposed by the directors:

15. That, the members of Celtic plc, noting the number of shareholders who have become untraced and whose dividend and other entitlements remain unclaimed, request the Board to appoint Georgeson, the asset reunification service operated by the Company's registrar, Computershare Investor Services PLC, to carry out a shareholder tracing and asset reunification programme on the customary contingent fee basis under which that service is provided at no upfront cost to the Company, and to report to shareholders on the programme at the next Annual General Meeting.

16. This AGM instructs the Board to prepare a strategic review and a published report with a football, financial, and strategic plan (medium term I.e. 3-5 years). The plan should contain a clear stated strategic aim and measurable football and financial goals for the Board to target. Remuneration should be linked to achieving those goals.

17. This AGM instructs the Chairman of the Board of Directors of Celtic PLC to:

17.1 Undertake, in cooperation with elected representatives of the Celtic support, a full review of the security operations at Celtic Park. The aim of such review to examine, among other things:

17.1.1 The training and management of security staff to assess their understanding of how best to ensure the safety and security of supporters.

17.1.2 The training and management of security staff to assess the extent to which medical emergencies are responded to appropriately.

17.1.3 Any systems intended to capture lessons from any incidents that do take place.

17.1.4 The recruitment of senior staff inside the security department; the extent to which they understand their role and the extent to which they are able to work with other departments (chiefly supporter liaison) to ensure the safety of supporters and their respectful treatment.

18. This AGM instructs the Chairman of the Board of Directors of Celtic PLC to:

18.1.1 Issue a full and unreserved apology to the shareholders and supporters of Celtic FC for giving a platform at the 2025 AGM to an individual, who holds no role within the governance of Celtic PLC, which he then abused to insult and denigrate our shareholders and our supporters.

18.1.2 To publicly commit to ensure that such an abuse of the AGM is never allowed to happen again.

The confirmation of the AGM plans come after fan groups called on Dermot Desmond to attend the AGM in person for the first time in 20 years.

A Celtic Fans Collective statement read: A Celtic Fans Collective statement read: "For twenty years, Dermot Desmond has not attended Celtic's Annual General Meeting, despite wielding considerable influence over the direction and decision-making of our club.

"Although only a minority shareholder, Desmond appears to exercise influence far beyond his shareholding. With that influence comes a responsibility to be accountable.

"We call on Dermot Desmond to publicly commit to attending the 2026 AGM in person and answer questions about his role in the running of Celtic Football Club.

"Sending his son, another representative or a prepared statement in his place is no substitute for attending personally.

"The decision by Peter Lawwell to prematurely conclude last year's AGM left a clear impression among supporters that the Board had taken an opportunity to avoid scrutiny. Responsibility for how that meeting was conducted and ultimately concluded rests entirely with the Board.

"This year, however, the focus must be firmly on scrutiny rather than protest. There is a clear understanding across the support that the AGM must provide the opportunity for important questions to be put directly to those running the Club, without allowing scrutiny to be evaded once again.

"Celtic supporters have repeatedly sought meaningful dialogue and a more constructive relationship with the Club.

"At a time when fans want to see decisive leadership, a public commitment from Dermot Desmond to attend the AGM in good faith would be an important demonstration of his willingness to engage directly with supporters and shareholders."

#2001. Auxerre vs. Paris FC - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 05 Nov 2026 07:12, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 07:14

Ten places separate Auxerre and Paris FC in the Ligue 1 table ahead of Saturday's matchday 10 fixture at Stade de l'Abbe-Deschamps.

Liam Rosenior's men could theoretically finish the weekend joint-top if they secure maximum points against the side with the division's worst defensive record and Paris Saint-Germain lose to Troyes.

Rosenior faced considerable criticism after his forgettable spell at Chelsea earlier this year, but the Englishman has Paris FC flying after nine matchdays.

Les Bleus sit fourth in the division with 17 points from a possible 27, level with third-placed Lyon, one behind second-placed Lille and just three adrift of local rivals PSG.

Much of their early-season success admittedly stems from their strong form at Stade Jean-Bouin, where they remain unbeaten after collecting 13 of a possible 15 points.

However, they have struggled to replicate those performances on their travels, losing half of their four away matches, including the last two against Lorient (1-0) and Lens (2-1).

Paris have not won away since early October's 3-2 success at Marseille, and a return of just four points from 12 on the road undermines their prospects of drawing level with PSG before Luis Enrique's men face Troyes later on Saturday.

Will Still's Auxerre have made a patchy start to the campaign, compounded by their failure to keep clean sheets in eight of their nine Ligue 1 fixtures.

The 14th-placed club's only shutout came in September's 1-0 victory over Nice, but Les Ajaistes have been unable to keep opponents at bay since.

That defensive weakness leaves Still's team vulnerable, and they enter Saturday's encounter having conceded 23 league goals, three more than bottom-placed Le Havre, further underlining their difficulties.

While their 13 goals exceed the totals of all but two bottom-half clubs, Brest (16) and Strasbourg (17), this weekend's hosts leave themselves with considerable work to do by conceding far too freely.

Nonetheless, eagle-eyed observers will note that Auxerre have conceded just five goals in front of their supporters while scoring as many themselves, offering encouragement ahead of matchday 10.

Given Paris' away struggles, Les Ajaistes, who have collected seven points from 12 on home soil, will back themselves to secure maximum points against Rosenior's high-flying side.

Lamfia Dioubate was dismissed after 11 minutes of the 5-1 defeat to Strasbourg last time out, leaving Auxerre without the midfielder.

While Sekou Fofana is touch-and-go due to a groin issue, Bryan Okoh, Remy Labeau Lascary and Assane Diousse are all sidelined for the hosts.

Cameron Archer leads Auxerre's scoring charts with six goals, three more than Danny Namaso, and the Englishman will aim to build on his prolific start to the campaign.

Paris, meanwhile, could be without Ligue 1's leading scorer Lassine Sinayoko, whose eight goals surpass everyone else's tally in the competition, while his five assists underline his dual threat.

Given that Sinayoko has scored half of Les Bleus' 16 league goals, the visitors may have to rely on alternative sources; only Maxime Lopez and Pablo Pagis have also scored more than once for Rosenior's side, leaving the manager short of proven match-winners.

Apart from Sinayoko, the capital club have several other injury doubts: Adama Camara (hamstring), Luca Koleosho (muscle), Jonathan Ikone (thigh) and Nhoa Sangui (muscle) could all miss out.

Nardi; Makosso, Tuanzebe, Akpa; Sy, Danois, Ahamada, Oppegard; Faivre, Namaso; Archer

Trapp; Traore, Chergui, Coppola, Otavio; Lopez, Lees Melou; Kebbal, Pagis, Simon; Sissoko

Auxerre's league-worst defensive record is concerning, but conceding just five goals across four home matches suggests that Saturday's assignment may be less straightforward than the table implies.

Paris have struggled to replicate their home performances on the road, and Sinayoko's potential absence could leave Rosenior's men settling for a point.

#1997. Arsenal suffer fresh injury blow as Mikel Arteta reveals "some issues" after Slavia Prague win

By Lewis Blain | 05 Nov 2026 07:21

Arsenal have suffered a potential injury setback after Ezri Konsa was forced off during their 2-1 win over Slavia Prague in the Champions League on Wednesday evening.

Mikel Arteta confirmed the England defender was substituted because of a fitness issue, having appeared to struggle with his knee during the match.

However, the Gunners have received a timely boost with William Saliba now fit and available again after recovering from a long-term back injury.

Konsa started alongside Gabriel in the heart of Arsenal's defence but was withdrawn shortly after the hour mark following a difficult second half.

The centre-back was spotted feeling his knee during the opening period before continuing after the interval, although he was eventually replaced by Arteta.

The Arsenal manager confirmed the substitution was fitness-related rather than tactical, explaining that the defender had been playing a considerable amount of football recently.

"Obviously he's playing a lot," Arteta said after the match, via the Evening Standard. "He's played so many games in the last few weeks. He had some issues, and we decided to take him off."

Konsa's fitness will now be monitored, particularly with Arsenal continuing to juggle their domestic and European commitments.

There was better news regarding William Saliba, however, with the Frenchman returning to the matchday squad after missing the start of the season with a back injury.

Before the match, Arteta confirmed that the 25-year-old had completed 45 minutes in a behind-closed-doors friendly without any setbacks, and claimed that "he feels ready to go" and "feels really comfortable."

Saliba's return could hardly have come at a better time for the Gunners, particularly with Konsa now carrying a potential injury concern.

The summer signing has hugely impressed alongside Gabriel, but having another established centre-back available means Arteta is not suddenly short of options.

There would be some risk in throwing Saliba straight back into the starting XI against Hull City on Saturday, especially after such a lengthy absence.

However, the upcoming fixture could offer a relatively favourable opportunity to gradually reintegrate the Frenchman, provided Arteta is satisfied with his fitness.

Konsa's situation will need assessing before any decisions are made, but Saliba's availability gives Arsenal some welcome defensive insurance at an important stage of the campaign.

#1995. Hearts player ratings as experienced duo suffer comical defensive blunders

Seriously let down by the players in front of him as he was helpless to avoid picking the ball out of his net on three occasions. Had made a handful of simple stops before being stumped by Jamie McCart's inexplicable own goal, and given no chance after Stephen Kingley teed up Thun for a second. The third was by him in a flash. Scoreline could have been worse if not for the keeper.

Shoehorned in at right-back due to Hearts' incredible misfortune with injuries. But gifted away the second goal as he only prodded into the path of Brighton Labeau, who slammed into net. Perhaps a natural right-footed player would have cleared easily, but no excuse for this mistake by an experienced player. Night only worsened by a suspected hamstring injury which forced him off.

Took a forearm to the jaw from Furkan Dursun in the first-half, for which the forward was only booked. Was then badly outmuscled by the forward who poked home a third for the hosts in Switzerland after getting in front of the defender. Centre-back did give travelling 2,000 Hearts fans something to cheer with terrific header into the bottom corner after rising highest at the backpost to net a consolation.

Was so close to scoring for Hearts in Trabzon last time out in this competition and was denied a headed goal again here, with Niklas Steffen producing a terrific low save to his left. Wasn't dominant or convincing enough in the rearguard for Hearts but that is criticism which can be levelled at the whole defence.

Another player forced into an uncomfortable position owing to the injury situation as he slotted into left back. Had started okay but came undone by a comical own goal as he got his feet mixed up and inadvertently diverted the ball into the bottom corner - had done well in rescuing his positioning before the horror blunder. Like Hearts, never truly recovered.

Drafted into midfield again and was one of the better performers in there, or at least one of the most involved. Carried a threat with his deliveries from set-pieces, resulting in a consolation from Stuart Findlay. He was industrious but not always the most effective in duels in midfield with Hearts overrun by the hosts.

One of few Hearts players who looked like doing something going forward. After 20 minutes he showed his ability as he cut inside to the edge of the box before unleashing a fierce strike to force a save. But he was too often neglected by his team-mates who moved the ball across the park instead of repeatedly shovelling to McPake who had the beating of his man.

Looked lively in the opening exchanges with some nice touches but his impact waned. He wasn't able to penetrate the Thun defence in his passing and was understandably frustrated when his press wasn't backed up by his team-mates in charging out from the back.

Hearts are a better team when Mendy is heavily involved in his all-action style, but that was missing against Thun. He cut a tired figure in the midfield and wasn't able to really dictate any play or take charge of the midfield battle as he was bypassed regularly by Thun.

A frustrating watch against Thun as he looked to pose a threat but could never really make it count. Often found in space and tasked with driving at the defence but his touch was slack on a handful of occasions and he was totally dominated by the impressive Olivier Mambwa who gave him very little room to do anything.

A long old night for the striker. Was always going to be a tough task with creativity lacking for Hearts for long periods but he couldn't make anything stick even when the ball reached him. Best moments came when he had support from JJ Williams but by then the game was out of Hearts' reach. Not a major chance of his own to speak of.

Pierre Landry Kabore (for Guendouz, 54) 5

Quickly involved in smart interplay with Braga as he made an instant, albeit not telling, impact. Threw himself about and put in a shift defensively, too.

A tremendous opportunity for the teenager, who has been on loan at Stenhousemuir. Made a crucial interception and smart pass seconds after coming on.

On to spearhead the attack for the final 15 minutes but was largely anonymous in this cameo outing as he continues to search for a spark after arriving at Hearts.

Another thrown on for the final period with the Thun lead looking insurmountable.

#1992. Enzo Maresca now doubles down on his Gianluigi Donnarumma stance after latest Man City "mistake"

By Lewis Blain | 05 Nov 2026 07:47

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has defended Gianluigi Donnarumma once again following another costly mistake during their 3-2 win over RB Leipzig in the Champions League on Wednesday evening.

The Italian goalkeeper was criticised after allowing Ridle Baku's effort to beat him at the near post, adding to a growing list of errors this season.

However, Maresca has shown little indication that he intends to reconsider his first-choice goalkeeper ahead of Saturday's trip to face Nottingham Forest at the City Ground in the Premier League.

Donnarumma came under scrutiny after City's latest Champions League victory, having been unable to prevent Baku from equalising shortly after half-time.

The mistake followed previous errors against Aston Villa and Paris Saint-Germain, raising questions about the 27-year-old's consistency since arriving at the Etihad Stadium.

However, Maresca insisted that the incident was not a major concern, highlighting the goalkeeper's ability to produce important saves at the other end.

"It's not a concern, but it's a mistake," the City manager told reporters, via the BBC. "He recognises, he knows that it's a mistake. And now, in 48 hours, we have Nottingham Forest away, and we need to be focused on that."

Maresca was also asked whether the upcoming international break could provide an opportunity to reconsider his goalkeeping options, but again defended Donnarumma.

"I'm not thinking about the goalkeeper situation," he said. "We're talking about a mistake, but a few minutes before, he's done a save that any keeper in the world, they're not going to do that save!"

The City boss added that Donnarumma knows his performance was "not good" enough but believes he will improve in the coming weeks.

Donnarumma's recent errors are becoming difficult to ignore, particularly given his struggles with distribution and dealing with crosses into the penalty area.

However, Maresca's options behind the Italian are not particularly convincing, making a change difficult to justify.

City allowed James Trafford to leave during the summer, despite the Englishman's potential, and arguably made their own situation more complicated by not retaining a capable alternative.

Geronimo Rulli remains the back-up, and despite penalty heroics against Brighton & Hove Albion in the Carabao Cup, Maresca has already made clear that Donnarumma is his undisputed first choice.

The Italian's shot-stopping ability is also a major asset, as demonstrated by several outstanding interventions this season.

Despite the mistakes, it is difficult to envisage Maresca dropping Donnarumma anytime soon. The 6 foot 5 shot-stopper needs to improve his consistency, but City may have to persist with him given their current alternatives.

#1991. FC Thun vs Hearts almost immediately halted as pyro smoke fills stadium

The Conference League match between FC Thun and Heart of Midlothian had to be halted almost immediately.

The match referee stopped the match with less than a minute played due to smoke filling the stadium in Switzerland.

Pyrotechnic devices had been set off in the home end of the stadium, leading to very poor visibility on the pitch.

The match had to be stopped until the smoke cleared. The delay lasted around eight minutes before play was resumed for the Euro clash.

A Hearts statement on social media read: "Well, we did kick-off, but the game was almost immediately stopped, due to smoke from pyrotechnic devices let off in the home end.

"Should be back underway in the next minute or so."

#1990. Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur

“It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca said, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”

His team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

Maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

Momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc

Marco Rose, their new manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he said. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”

His team showed an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, new signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

They could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his new manager.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6

City will need more, especially in midfield. Anderson at his best can cover the ground and roles of two men, which is just as well as City await reinforcements. The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a big ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “new Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

There was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca said “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

Of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a new season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

Marc Guéhi: Central Midfield Edition pic.twitter.com/ViBZqOroB2

The Maresca era begins with the most dramatic of wins. City were trailing 1-0 at 84 minutes, but somehow managed to turn it around.

Emery doesn’t hang around. I’m not convinced he shook Hurzeler’s hand.

Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1 (Gvardiol) Oh my, Gvardiol has the ball in the back of the net but his “winner” is ruled out by the linesman instantly. Cherki had wriggled this way and that on the edge of the box before sliding in the Croatian who dispatched the ball with aplomb.

BUT, replays show that Hill’s back foot played Gvardiol onside ...so the late, late goal is GIVEN!

Maresca jumps for joy, the Etihad erupts. But that is heartbreaking for Bournemouth...

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur

Guehi saves the day for City, scoring a harder header than the sitter he missed early in this half. Nice corner from Cherki was powererd in from close to the penalty spot. Crowd smells blood with five minutes left but Bournemouth look to still have a bit in the tank.

Incidentally, Jack Grealish is on for City with the ‘Guernsey Grealish’ Alex Scott still out there for Bournemouth, who is presumably worth about double in today’s transfer market? Can’t be often that a player shares pitch with his nickname-giver as their careers head in opposite direction. Wonder if Lionel Messi was ever described as “the new Roman Riquelme?” and played against him?

Bournemouth have responded well to getting pegged back, playing through City, who are desperate for a shot at three points. Gannon-Doak stands up a cross but finds the gloves of Donnarumma.

City attempt to break down the left but Grealish just runs out of road.

Manchester City 1 Bournemouth 1 (Guehi) He might have missed a sitter earlier on, but when presented with a similar opportunity from a corner - this time via Cherki from the right - Guehi makes no mistake, planting his header beyond Petrovic.

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6

Haaland threatens to break free down Bournemouth’s right but Truffert just about recovers and clears his lines.

Grealish replaces Foden, who slopes straight down the tunnel.

Jebbison calls Donnarumma - who has been a spectator for the past 20 minutes - into action with a sharp header. There is a delay in the taking of the subsequent corner as Adams and Jebbison jostle for position with the City goalkeeper, but it’s all for nothing as the delivery is dealt with.

Foden goes into the book for a foul on substitute Jebbison. A tad harsh, perhaps. Looks like he semi-slipped into that contact.

Ayari attempts an bicycle kick but cannot beat Bizot. That would have been a goal of the month contender had it found the back of the net.

Guehi combines with Foden down the right and hits the by-line before a digging out a cross to Haaland. The ball is behind him and his right-footed effort does not have the requisite power to beat Petrovic, who has been immense today.

Bit better from City, Foden curls just wide, Semenyo has a shot well saved by Petrovic. Meres presence of Cherki seems to have injected some urgency to their attacks and fear to Bournemouth’s defence. Not sure City look quite ready for this season. Obviously there will be further incomings but they are leggier and more haphazard than Bournemouth.

Chance! Foden, Nunes and Cherki work the ball from right to left on the edge of Bournemouth’s box, eventually falling to Haaland who scoops the ball over with his usually lethal left boot. The visitors had plenty of men between ball and goal and that caused the Norwegian to snatch at his effort.

Villa started last season with no win in their first five games and just three points. They then rallied strongly after that. This one feels different as the rebuild is so significant. Second half has been very flat so far.

City are asking questions now. Cherki combines with Foden down the right and the Englishman shifts the ball on to his favoured left boot and his curled effort deflects off Silva and out for a corner which comes to nothing.

Semenyo breaks free down the left channel and fires the ball across the keeper towards the far post, but Petrovic gets a strong hand to it and pulls off a good save.

Kostoulas thinks he’s made it five having followed in a fizzed-in Costinha effort that had struck the post. But the strike is scrubbed off immediately and replays back up the linesman’s decision.

Little sign of City finding the composure to take control of this match. Passing is getting ever-sloppier and Guehi put a free header painfully wide. Maresca’s team are dominating possession but would be no surprise if the next goal was another Bournemouth sucker-punch. Kovacic and Cherki about to come on, the latter should improve the picture.

Anderson receives treatment on the pitch and is subsequently replaced by Kovacic. The Englishman stretches out his right leg as he leaves the field of play and keeps it elevated as he takes his position on the bench.

Dunk creates some chaos in Villa’s box, spinning in a lofted through-ball which Bizot palms away under duress. Rutter then pulls an effort wide off the resulting corner.

Nunes makes an instant impact, beating Scott easily down the right before standing up a cross to the far post where Haaland is waiting. Two Bournemouth defenders mirror the forward’s leap and do enough to disrupt his flow - and Semenyo’s - the Ghanaian also misses the ball.

Shows how few options Emery has - he has not made a change at half-time. Villa have been a little brighter going forward. A good run from Hemmings to play in Maatsen, and then the Villa teenager misjudging a cross when McGinn put him in down the right. But Brighton will feel there are more goals for them.

Maresca looks to his bench and brings on Nunes for Lewis.

Brighton are still going for this. Gross’ corner from the left reaches Vuskovic at the back post, but he cannot poke the ball past Bizot.

You’ll do well to see a worse miss all season! Guehi is afforded the freedom of Manchester inside the box from an inswinging corner but he somehow glances the ball wide.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP

De Cuyper tees up another corner from the right. His punched-in delivery picks out Ayari perfectly on the edge of the box but the Swede’s volley flies just wide. A touch ball to hit first time.

Villa have opted to sit in and hope they can see this out without further damage. The Sky Sports cameras pan to a now sparse away end where some are still cheering their side on. Fair play.

Play has resumed at the Etihad and immediately City begin circulating the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure. It’s all very slow still and they are unable to penetrate their opponents’ robust mid-black.

Boos at half time as City leave the field, although will charitably assume they are more for referee Jared Gillet for his late non-award of a penalty. Rico Lewis went down in the box but it looked soft. Another early test for Maresca, Bournemouth are lively in attack and defending capably. City all pace and intent but not playing with much patience or finesse.

Pretty horrifying first half from Villa. It was a strange team to start with – factoring in the four big summer sales and then the two absentees, Watkins and Emi Martinez. But this has been even worse than expected. Many of the team has just crumbled under the first sign of pressure. Pau Torres has been terrible. Joao Gomes picked up a yellow and then a red card on his debut. Villa started with Buendia as a centre-forward and now - with ten men - are just trying to play without any striker at all. Emery’s options are limited. Funny to think they started really well and should have taken the lead through Buendia on five minutes.

There’s a shout for a penalty as Haaland knocks down a header at the back post for Lewis, who gets shoved to the ground clumsily by Scott. Nothing going though, and that’s the half.

There’s a coming together on the halfway line at the Etihad. Haaland and Silva tangle, which sets off a chain reaction as Kluivert comes steaming in, first towards Haaland and then Guehi. Evanilson is next on the scene and he gets a firm shove off Gvardiol.

City now looking shaky at the back. Cross-field balls in their half zipping past half a dozen in sky blue without intervention, shots from range going just wide, Donnarumma needing to save well to prevent a second.

Has stopped clicking up front as well, something isn’t going to plan when you have Haaland in your team but most of the high balls are heading towards Foden and O’Reilly.

CARTÃO VERMELHO! Gomes is sent off. Disaster for Villa. It was a kick at Rutter borne of frustration. McGinn was already walking Gomes away from referee Peter Bankes before the decision came. A clear kick to the chest after Rutter knocked him over. Gomes has been nowhere near the level required. He will never forget his Villa debut.

Ooof, Tavernier goes close with a lovely curled effort from 25 yards out. Just wide, however.

Kluivert gets a sight at goal moments later but is denied by Donnarumma who gets down to his left sharply to keep the ball out.

Haaland looks to breathe life into City’s rather drab performance by chasing down Petrovic.

Moments later, he directs a glancing header towards goal and forces the Bournemouth keeper into a smart stop. Foden’s subsequent corner is not up to much.

VAR is looking at an incident on the halfway line. Rutter barges into Gomes and the midfielder kicks out at the Brighton front man. The referee is sent to the screen and a red card correctly follows. A dreadful performance from Gomes.

Villa have really struggled under pressure at the back. Going forward they still look have enough creative players that they are not embarrassed. But Brighton are dominating them with the press in the Villa half. There are not many options for Emery to change at half-time. Mings? Garnacho?

Some very untidy defending for the opening goal here which comes against the run of play, if not drastically so. Khusanov was bamboozled by an  innocuous high ball, couldn’t make decisive contact and left space for it to reach Evanlison on the right, whose cross was hard for Tavernier to miss.

A few groans and grumbles already from the home fans, Guehi getting some flak for squandering a decent position near the Bournemouth area and giving away the ball. Not really his job to be on the ball and making stuff happen near the opposition box though, is it?

This is looking very bad for Villa. Two Brighton goals in one minute for Jack Hinshelwood and it is 4-0 with 31 mins played. The first was a very well-worked goal – Ayari cross nodded down by Gomez for Hinshelwood to head in. The second was just another mistake by Villa – Ayari stealing the ball from Joao Gomes to create a critical turnover. Villa started well but they look completely outgunned physically. Brighton are really pressing home their advantage in the duels. Lots of pressure on the likes of young George Hemmings and Gomes.

"Absolutely INCREDIBLE!"Jack Hinshelwood scores two in a matter of minutes and Brighton are ripping Aston Villa apart! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tvS5qMJJ8C

Brighton 4 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) That’s two in a matter of seconds. Again, Villa try to play out from the back and again they get caught out. Ayari telescopes in a leg to take the ball away from Gomes on the edge of Villa’s box and Hinshelwood is there to tuck it home.

Brighton 3 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) A cross from the left is nodded back across goal by Gomez and Hinshelwood is there to finish.

Manchester City 0 Bournemouth 1 (Tavernier) Bournemouth carve City open with ease. A long ball from Smith is not dealt with and Rayan works the ball out to Evanilson who needs just a brief look up before picking out Tavernier, who finishes at the back post.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc

City have not yet reached the intensity levels they usually show when in full swing. Semenyo tries to inject some energy with a burst down the left but Rayan does well to track back and cut it out.

Villa’s defence is floundering. This time a corner delivered from the right sails over everyone, including Bizot, but the back-post nod-down evades everyone and Villa clear their lines.

Bright start from City, but momentum has diminished since an odd miss from Haaland, whose limbs looked unusually muddled after O’Reilly soared down the left wing and crossed presentably. Move had an air of inevitability to it, was unexpected not to see the Norwegian score. Prepare the Samson similes.

The second goal from Brighton, and it’s direct. Georginio Rutter played through with a very straight ball, and Rutter had Pau Torres on the proverbial toast. De Cuyper kept up with his team-mate and ran onto the cross. Villa have not been bad. Torres, however, is having a dreadful afternoon.

Brighton 2 Aston Villa 0 (De Cuyper) Rutter does brilliantly to latch on to a ball over the top from well inside his half. He bursts down the left channel before lashing a fierce ball across the face of goal which De Cuyper turns in. Villa in all sorts of problems here.

What a start for Brighton!Maxim De Cuyper doubles their advantage! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/3WbyZlEhMV

Chance! O’Reilly bursts past Smith out on the left and picks out Haaland, who appears to be in two minds as to whether he wants to head or volley the ball. Instead he does neither and the chance goes begging.

Gomes leaves one on Ayari, which is risky given he has already picked up a booking. A red card at this point would be hugely damaging.

Brighton take the lead with an own goal from Victor Lindelof. An unfortunate one for the Swede who was trying to get Maxim De Cuyper’s shot off the line. It hit the post and ricocheted in off Lindelof. The fault lay with Pau Torres who gave the ball away needlessly. Very good turn from De Cuyper to make the room for the shot. Up until then, Villa - even with this unusual understrength side - were much the better.

Lewis is in fact playing right-back, with Guehi into defensive midfield alongside Anderson. O’Reilly advanced of both, with Gvardiol at left-back. All quite fluid, though, as you would expect from modern City.

Brighton 1 Aston Villa 0 (OG Lindelof) A disaster at the back for Villa. Pau Torres looks to play out from near the by-line but instead picks out De Cuyper inside Villa’s box. The wide man does well to steady himself before getting a shot away, which ricochets off the post, back on to Lindelof and into the net.

City have started brightly. Here Haaland slips in Lewis, who is unmissable with his new bleached hair, but Petrovic pulls off a smart save.

Chance! Ayari gets his pocket picked inside his own half by a buzzing Barkley. Buendia has a sight of goal but he slides the ball inches wide.

He’s at it again moments later, but he sends a third effort at goal over the bar.

Villa have started the brighter of the two sides. McGinn spins a deep free-kick into the box, which is cleared out to Buendia on the edge of the box but his shot sails over.

A warm minute’s applause for the former Manchester City manager.

Brighton are in their customary blue and white home kits shooting left to right, with Villa in black.

That’s a “Welcome Back Enzo” banner slowly cascading down the East stand. Feel that the tifo department has missed a trick, because it would have been very amusing to use a picture of Pep Guardiola, and see if anyone noticed. That could actually be Guardiola for all I know, my facial recognition is dreadful. Getting all of the trite “don’t they look similar!” observations out of my system ahead of the September cut-off point.

The teams have emerged from the tunnel at the Amex and the Etihad...

When asked by Sky Sports whether Ollie Watkins’ omission from the match-day squad was a sign that his Villa career was over, Emery pursed his lips and stared back at the reporter for a few seconds before saying: “Silence.”

After being pressed on the subject, he added: “No, no, no. We are playing today here. It’s OK. We are not speaking about [Ollie].”

"Silence" 🤫An unusual response from Unai Emery 😅 pic.twitter.com/kWNZtQu3PA

On taking charge of his first match as City head coach, Enzo Maresca told Sky Sports: “It’s big emotion. It’s a very nice feeling, the first game at home in front of our fans, so hopefully we can give them the three points.”

When asked about Elliot Anderson and the void left by Rodri, he added: “I think Elliot [Anderson] has to be himself; a good player, he’s going to be even better, but he has to be himself. Again, for me, there are no players that they are the same player, they are all different.

“We are happy with Elliot, but for sure, as we know, Rodri is a big player but he’s already gone. So now the focus is on the ones that are here with us and the ones that will probably arrive.”

Brighton and Hove Albion Verbruggen; Wieffer, Vuskovic, Boscagli, Dunk; Gross, Ayari; Gomez, Hinshelwood, De Cuyper; Rutter

Subs Steele, Strujik, Costinha, Svoboda, Osman, Yalcouye, David, Kostoulas, Yohanna

Aston Villa Bizot; Cash, Torres, Lindelof, Maatsen; Barkley, Kamara; McGinn, Gomes, Hemmings; Buendia

Subs Suzuki, Mings, Ruggeri, Bogarde, Alysson, Rowe, Burrowes, Garnacho, Lynch

Manchester City Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Lewis; Semenyo, Foden, O’Reilly; Haaland

Subs Rulli, Ait-Nouri, Nunes, Reis, Kovacic, Cherki, Gonzalez, Grealish, Marmoush

Bournemouth Petrovic; Smith, Silva, Hill, Truffert; Cook, Scott; Rayan, Kluivert, Tavernier; Evanilson

Subs Dennis, Diakite, Gannon-Doak, Toth, Sanchez, Brooks, Adams, Rodriguez, Jebbison

Brighton have spent around £100m this summer but of those only the Croatian centre-back, Luka Vušković, is in the starting XI to face Aston Villa. He cost £46m from Spurs. Brighton have, as ever, sold players with Jan-Paul Van Hecke the biggest price. The expectation is that Carlos Baleba will leave for Manchester United. He is not in the squad. The injured Yankuba Minteh would not have been involved today - but he is another likely departure. Player of the year Ferdi Kadioglu is missing with injury.

Pep Guardiola’s successor assessed the breadth of the challenge before him and offered a candid appraisal of how to replace the irreplaceable. “It would be silly to try and change it,” he said of Guardiola’s grand design.

Tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s big idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

Describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

The Villa team is missing six of the players who started the Europa League final against Freiburg on May 20. Four of them have left (Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans) and Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins might be leaving too - they are absent today. Belgian goalkeeper Marco Bizot starts and there is also a place for teenager George Hemmings. Emi Buendia in what looks like the central striker role. It is certainly a bracing opening day to the season for Unai Emery.

No sign of Watkins in what is an objectively underpowered Aston Villa line-up. There’s also no start for new signing Suzuki, with Emery preferring Bizot between the sticks. Academy graduate Hemmings makes his first Premier League start.

Representing Aston Villa 👊 pic.twitter.com/JjqgYhBzwb

TEAM NEWS! 🚨 Here's how we start 🆚 Villa! 👊 pic.twitter.com/nnFj5swsdg

Some eyebrows raised at the inclusion of Rico Lewis in City’s starting XI, presumably as a defensive midfielder given the presence of Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly and Khusanov on the team-sheet. He did not have a pleasant afternoon in Cardiff last weekend, although that could be said for several City players. Some lingering doubts about his physicality, in a Premier League becoming ever more hands-on, but Enzo Maresca knows him from his time as an assistant here and clearly rates him. Wonder whether that sentiment will endure if (when) City buy some new midfielders in the coming weeks.

🔵 TEAM NEWS🍒The first #afcb team of the new Premier League season 👊 pic.twitter.com/uJhTI01Jld

Haaland will make his 200th appearance for City this afternoon. Either Lewis or O’Reilly could be deployed alongside Anderson in central midfield.

Our first XI of the season! 🩵XI | Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias (C), Guéhi, Gvardiol, Lewis, Anderson, O'Reilly, Semenyo, Foden, HaalandSUBS | Rulli, Marmoush, Kovačić, Cherki, Nico, Grealish, Aït-Nouri, Reis, Nunes🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/6wSBoP8jon

Welcome to live coverage of Sunday afternoon’s 2pm Premier League kick-offs. Enzo Maresca faces the unenviable task of following Pep Guardiola’s decade of dominance at Manchester City and his reign begins in earnest with a visit from Bournemouth, who themselves are ushering in a new era after Marco Rose succeeded Andoni Iraola. A bruising 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield last weekend does not bode well for City’s hopes of closing the gap to Arsenal, but Maresca will be telling his charges that this afternoon is a fresh start: a new week and a new competition, plus Erling Haaland has a new haircut…

The Italian’s squad has been shorn of World Cup winner Rodri, who departed for Barcelona this week, and the spotlight will turn to £116m club-record signing Elliot Anderson who is expected to make his Premier League debut with City. Jérémy Doku is out for two to three weeks after suffering a calf injury, which could open the door for Jack Grealish, with City bereft of wide options. City will have their work cut out as Bournemouth, fresh off a historic sixth-place finish last season, look to extend their 18-match unbeaten run from the end of last season. The Cherries won three of their five pre-season matches, which included an eye-catching 10-1 victory over Serie A side Genoa.

Brighton and Hove Albion welcome Aston Villa to the Amex for their 2026-27 season opener having travelled 220 miles north of the Arctic Circle to play Norwegian side Tromso in their Europa Conference league play-off on Thursday. Fabian Hurzeler’s side face the defending Europa League champions without Carlos Baleba, who is on the brink of joining Manchester United, as well as injured wingers Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh. While Unai Emery has lost key players in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, the funds raised has gone towards seven signings, with Zion Suzuki, the Japan goalkeeper, in line to make his first start for Villa.

#1989. Cardinale: “Milan were at the top of the world, and we’re going to bring them back there”

AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale spoke to CBS Sports before the derby win over Inter, pledging to bring the club back to the summit of football.

On Halloween night, the Rossoneri ensured that Inter’s derby nightmare continued as Milan won their fourth consecutive victory in the fixture, extending the unbeaten run against the Nerazzurri to eight meetings in the process.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

All of the damage was done in the first half. Christian Pulisic struck in the fourth minute with a header, Adrien Rabiot scored from a corner six minutes later, Alessandro Bastoni halved the deficit and then Diego Moreira converted a lovely free-kick to reopen the two-goal advantage.

In the end, 3-1 is how it would stay, securing a memorable win. Cardinale spoke with the CBS panel in the build-up to kick-off at San Siro last night and he shed a bit more light on his plans for the Rossoneri moving forward. His words are via MilanNews.

“Well, first of all, this stadium… As an American, I can say that a stadium like this is something you never see anywhere else. Tonight, it’s going to light up. There’s something different about this derby tonight than in the past.

“There’s an electricity here that I’ve never felt before. You’ll see nearly 80,000 people literally shaking this structure. It’s going to be truly incredible.”

“It is. You know, when we bought the club four years ago, I started working on this right away. And part of what we’re trying to do here is bring the best of America to Italian soccer, and specifically to AC Milan.

“It’s extraordinary: most people didn’t think we could accomplish all this, or even get to this point. Not only did we announce the stadium this week, but we also announced the largest naming rights deal in history. I think it’s a wonderful thing for Italian soccer.

“The message to everyone is that we’re coming back. Italian soccer truly deserves to be at the top again, and we’ll do everything we can through AC Milan to make that happen.”

“There’s a connection between us. We’re two guys from Pennsylvania trying to make their way and understand Italy. He’s ‘Captain America’, but he’s also my franchise player. I couldn’t be more thrilled to have him with us.

“It’s a true partnership with him. He’s a leader, and his presence on the court makes all the difference in the world. You’ve seen it this year: when he steps on the court, he completely changes the game.”

Why is AC Milan and winning with Milan so important to you?

“I remember George Steinbrenner telling me about twenty years ago, ‘Don’t get too emotionally involved in all this; don’t go into the locker room, don’t do those things’. But in this case, I got emotionally involved.

“For me, it became a personal issue. And I don’t know what it is: maybe it’s just that… look around, listen. This means so much to the people of Milan, it has a huge impact on them, and I feel a huge responsibility.

“AC Milan were at the top of the world, and we’re going to bring them back there. This will probably be one of the greatest things I’ll do in my career.”

“It’s something multigenerational. This stadium is an icon. Look around, look at these people: this means everything to them. All of this carries with it an enormous amount of responsibility, it almost makes your wrists tremble.

“The best thing I can do is do my job well to help this club win, because victory spreads to the whole community. Listen… can you hear? That’s the Curva. You don’t see anything like it in America, it’s truly special.”

What’s your favourite detail of the new stadium?

“What we tried to do with the new stadium was to live up to the name and tradition of this facility. This is San Siro, but it is also ‘La Scala del Calcio’, the opera house of football.

“When you look at the design of the new stadium, those majestic, slender lines on the exterior recall the grand drapes and curtains of La Scala. It is our tribute to the history of this city.”

How did you manage to unblock the stadium situation?

“It’s been an incredible collaboration, a true partnership with our president Paolo Scaroni and the mayor. It’s extraordinary because everyone told me it’s impossible to build a stadium here in Italy. The last major stadium built in Italy was in 2011 in Turin, with about 40,000 seats.

“The extraordinary thing about our project is that it will be a 75,000-seat stadium, and we expect to have it completed before the 2032 European Championships. It will be a great thing for all of Italy.”

#1985. Nottingham Forest vs Manchester City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 05 Nov 2026 08:00, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 08:08

Second from bottom faces second from top in the Premier League on Saturday evening, as Nottingham Forest welcome Manchester City to the City Ground.

The two teams played out a 2-2 draw in their last meeting at the Etihad Stadium in March, with Elliot Anderson scoring a late equaliser for Forest before completing his big-money move to City in the summer.

Man City strengthened their hopes of securing automatic qualification for the Champions League last 16 with a 3-2 away victory over RB Leipzig on Wednesday, climbing into seventh place in the 36-team League Phase table at the halfway stage.

Manager Enzo Maresca has admitted that his team “struggled” in moments against Leipzig, but the German club’s nemesis Erling Haaland – wearing the captain’s armband – was on hand to slide home a 78th-minute match-winner for City and his 13th goal in just nine games against Die Roten Bullen.

The Citizens were made to work for their victory over Leipzig having previously suffered back-to-back Premier League defeats to Aston Villa and Brighton & Hove Albion, results that forced them to surrender top spot in the table to champions Arsenal.

City’s 24-game scoring streak in the Premier League was halted by a high-flying Seagulls side who battled to a narrow 1-0 victory at the Etihad last weekend, despite Maresca’s men registering 21 shots worth 1.92 expected goals (xG) and over 60% possession.

Not since February/March 2016 under Manuel Pellegrini have Man City lost three PL games in a row, and they head to the City Ground this weekend having won two of their previous four league visits (D1 L1) since Forest’s return to the top flight in 2022, most recently winning 2-1 in December last year.

Oliver Glasner has not made the desired impact as Nottingham Forest head coach, with his team winning only one of their opening nine Premier League games (D3 L5) and accumulating just a single point from their last 15 available, leaving them down in 19th place in the table.

Scoring goals has been the key issue for the Tricky Trees, who are the Premier League’s joint-lowest scorers (six) and have drawn a blank in five of their nine matches, despite registering the second-most shots per game in the division (16.9), only behind Manchester United (18.6).

A further 15 shots and just one on target in the 78th minute was recorded in last weekend’s 2-0 defeat at Brentford - another frustrating result that sparked a passionate post-match rant from Glasner, demanding his players to 'either buy in to changes or leave' to ensure that last season’s “s*** situation” does not repeat itself.

Forest’s hierarchy have reportedly welcomed Glasner’s strong words, but the real test is whether his misfiring squad will finally respond on the pitch. The Tricky Trees remains winless and goalless in five home fixtures this season, losing their last two to Coventry and Arsenal by a 1-0 scoreline.

Glasner now faces a daunting task against Man City, having lost four of his previous five league meetings with them (D1) during his time as Crystal Palace boss, conceding at least three goals in each defeat. However, Forest can draw confidence from their 1-0 home victory over City just two seasons ago, thanks to a late Callum Hudson-Odoi strike.

Nottingham Forest form (all competitions):

Nottingham Forest midfielder Nicolas Dominguez (muscle) and forward Igor Jesus (calf) are both doubtful, while defender Nicolo Savona (knee) remains sidelined with a long-term injury.

Former Man City youngster Liam Delap has failed to score in his last five starts for Forest and is at risk of losing his centre-forward spot to Chris Wood, who is still waiting to start hist first league game of the season.

James McAtee – another ex-City player – has made a notable impression in a deeper midfield role where he is expected to continue, while Daniel Munoz and Ousmane Diomande will both be pushing for recalls in defence.

As for Man City, Maresca is not expected to make wholesale changes, but captain Ruben Dias and Josko Gvardiol are strong contenders to earn a recall in defence at the expense of Marc Guehi and Nico O'Reilly.

Enzo Fernandez, who scored his first UCL goal for City in midweek, is the most likely midfielder to play alongside Anderson, though Ayyoub Bouaddi and Mateo Kovacic are two central options pushing to replace the Argentine.

Haaland – without a goal in his last four appearances against Forest – will lead the line once again and could be supported in attack by Iliman Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Jeremy Doku, the latter of whom began as a substitute against Leipzig.

Nottingham Forest possible starting lineup:

Sels; Cunha, Milenkovic, Murillo; Munoz, McAtee, Schlager, Williams; Ndoye, Gibbs-White; Delap

Manchester City possible starting lineup:

Donnarumma; Nunes, Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol; Anderson, Fernandez; Ndiaye, Cherki, Doku; Haaland

Forest’s misfiring frontline is a growing concern for Glasner, but the hosts should take encouragement from Man City’s porous defence that has conceded 14 goals in their last seven games in all competitions.

A closely-contested battle could be in store this weekend, but we expect the Citizens to possess the clinical edge required to claim maximum points.

#1983. Virtus Verona 2-3 Milan Futuro: Menon, Perera and Pagliei score in entertaining win

Milan Futuro are back in the win column as they managed to secure a thrilling 3-2 victory away against Virtus Verona.

Milan Futuro battled hard against Pavonese in the rearranged Serie D matchday six fixture on Wednesday night and got a 1-1 draw away from home, despite having gone down to 10 men. It was a result to build on, and build on it they did.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

After a tentative start in which both teams had a few half-chances, it was the home team took the lead in the 20th minute with a shot from outside the box by Cuel that deceived Pittarella.

The Rossoneri equalised in the 22nd minute through Luca Menon, who beat the opposing goalkeeper with a powerful left-footed shot from the edge of the box. After the equaliser, both teams had opportunities to go ahead, but it was level at the break.

The Rossoneri got off to a much better start in the second half, taking the lead in the 49th minute after a persistent attack through Nirash Perera, who volleyed in a fine cross from the right.

Navarro’s team then made it 3-1 in the 73rd minute with Matteo Pagliei, who headed in a great Lorenzo Ossola cross. The home side made it a one-goal game again in the 78th minute through Franchi, but it wasn’t enough.

The Futuro therefore return to winning ways in the league and climbs to 17 points in the standings, with the second half of the match against Piacenza still to be played after that was suspended due to the referee getting injured.
